subject: For everyone who said “I’m in” (and for those who didn’t)
body:
November 23, 2026 | Read Online ( https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/8kux2dwlvquoh30gnl8akhkk009rlt3hkx9g5/x0hph6heg3l707s5hl/aHR0cHM6Ly9ja2FyY2hpdmUuY29tL2IvNHp1dmhlaDk1MDhyM3U2b3Z2ZW9sYTY2bm43MmVzNWg0ZzB6bA== )

-->True the Vote

From Catherine
--------------

Support True the Vote’s work ( https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/8kux2dwlvquoh30gnl8akhkk009rlt3hkx9g5/6qheh8hlqod2eptohk/aHR0cHM6Ly90cnVldGhldm90ZS5vcmcvZG9uYXRl )

Hi Friend —

Happy Thanksgiving week! I hope you find a little time to slow down and enjoy the people you love. As I count my blessings, I want you to know you’re among them. Thank you for all you do.

Over the past few weeks, so many of you have written to say, “I’m in.” There’s a little leap of faith in those two words, especially when the work ahead feels daunting — so, if you’ve ever wondered how much difference one person can really make, this Thanksgiving story is for you.

Most of us know the story of the Pilgrims and the Wampanoag Indians sharing a harvest feast at Plymouth in 1621. Then, between 1790 and 1862, presidents called for national days of thanksgiving on several occasions. George Washington designated February 19, 1795, as a day of thanksgiving and prayer. In April 1815, James Madison called on Americans to give thanks for peace after the War of 1812. And in April 1862, Lincoln asked Americans to give thanks for Union victories at their next worship services.

But what Americans still lacked was one day they could count on sharing every year. Thanksgiving with a capital “T”.

God put that idea on the heart of a magazine editor named Sarah Hale.

For fifteen years, Sarah made the case in print and in letters to governors across the country. Americans in every state, she believed, ought to be able to set aside the same day each year to give thanks together.

Imagine what it took for Sarah to pick up that pen year after year as the divide in the country she loved grew deeper and deeper. Then came the war. Family against family. Brother against brother. Still, she didn’t quit. She believed Americans could give thanks to God together, even then.

One day she wrote one more letter — and it changed all of our lives.

That letter, dated September 28, 1863, was addressed to President Abraham Lincoln. Five days later, he invited Americans to give thanks together on the last Thursday of November. Every president since has renewed that invitation to Thanksgiving Day.

All because of the perseverance of one person.

Maybe you’ve seen something in your own community that ought to change. And maybe you’re the one who will stay with it long enough to see that change through, leaving our grandchildren to wonder how it was ever any other way.

One woman’s persistence helped give a divided nation a day to give thanks. The next time you wonder what difference you can make, I hope you’ll remember her.

Another interesting bit of trivia — the Thanksgiving Day Sarah asked Americans to share in 1863 fell on November 26. This year, so does ours.

Thursday, when I bow my head, I’ll give thanks for many, many things. I’ll thank God for all those who came before us and gave us a country to be thankful for. And I’ll thank Him for each of you who looked at the work ahead and said, “I’m in.” You give me great hope.

Keep the faith. Never quit. Isaiah 6:8 is for you. Ephesians 6 FTW!

Ever onward —

Father,

Thank You for Your countless blessings. Thank You for our families and our friends. Thank You for our communities, our churches, and our nation. Thank You for the beauty of Your creation, for Your Word that guides our steps, and for Your constant presence that never leaves us. Thank You for the hope we have in Your promises.

Thank You for Your love. And may Your love flow through us. Help us to reflect love in the way we live, the way we treat others, and the way we worship You. Remind us that love is the root of everything we do.

But above all, Father, thank You for Jesus. Thank You for loving us so deeply that You sent Your One and Only Son to bear the punishment that belonged to us. Thank You for His willingness to endure the cross so that we could be forgiven, redeemed, and set free. Help us to never lose sight of the incredible gift we have been given through Him and may we never take for granted the love and sacrifice of our Savior.

In Jesus' Name, Amen!

~Jenna Riggs

For more prayers and encouragement from Jenna, join our Devotionals Space ( https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/8kux2dwlvquoh30gnl8akhkk009rlt3hkx9g5/8ghqhoho49x5nrikh9/aHR0cHM6Ly9jb21tdW5pdHkudHR2bm93Lm9yZy9jL2Rldm90aW9uYWxzLw== ) in the TTVN Community!

Until Next Week
---------------

Remember: you don't need a title, a law degree, or anyone's permission to get involved. You need awareness, courage, and the resolve to stay in it when others walk away.

True the Vote will keep doing our part. With faith as our foundation and patriots like you standing in the gap, we'll keep pressing for transparency, accountability, and an America we leave stronger than we found it.

Ever onward.

name: Mark Ronchetti
subject: You get a 10-minute head start. Now what?
body:
Plus: Trump is frustrated with JD Vance, and it is getting worse | New episode for dpwillis67@gmail.com

| | | | | |
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/r3zSGCPo8FN?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
| | | | | | It has been a week! Microsoft went down. Every flight in the country got grounded. Four big banks had problems, United’s computers quit, the NSA’s internal network went dark, and then Apple. It has felt like three months, and we haven’t even mentioned the stock market yet.
Nobody has shown that any of it is connected. [But Costco is selling out of generators, and we spent a good part of this show figuring out how much getting ready is enough. ](https://us.list-manage.com/wd6yS3dFZcM?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)Then there’s Trump and JD Vance, which is getting ugly faster than we thought it would.
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/1BYZ7PJvoU2?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
| | 🔦 **GENERATORS ARE SELLING OUT AT COSTCO, AND WE HAD TO FIGURE OUT WHERE OUR LINE IS**
As of last Sunday, 21 of the 26 big generators on Costco’s website were gone, including one that costs $7,000. Do we all need one of those?
Our number one worry is how to reach our daughter at college if the phones don’t work. So we stocked up on water, got a couple weeks of food together, and did not buy out the toilet paper aisle. We’re not bunker people, and nobody in this house is canning.
But what would you do with a 10-minute head start before everything shuts off? Stay in the city or get out?

🤖 **ONE STORY SAYS THE OUTAGES COULD ACTUALLY BE GOOD NEWS**
Josh Hawley says if this is all a coincidence, it’s the greatest coincidence in the history of the world. That’s what everybody is thinking.
But the New York Post has a different take. Companies are using AI to hunt for holes in their own software, AI is finding a whole lot more than anybody expected, and the rush to fix them is what’s knocking things offline. We’re not telling you that’s the answer. It’s the first explanation that sounded plausible to both of us.
---
| [STREAM NOW](https://us.list-manage.com/17SqH0eh6nc?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
---
| | 🇺🇸 **TRUMP IS FRUSTRATED WITH JD VANCE, AND IT’S GOING TO GET WORSE**
After the midterms, JD Vance said the Iran war is why Republicans lost. Trump agreed with him at first. Now he’s telling people Vance should have added that going in was the right call.
Here’s the problem. JD doesn’t believe that, and he never has. So he’s got nowhere to go. And when somebody had to stand up this week and tell the country not to be scared about the outages, it wasn’t the vice president. It was Marco Rubio. Again.
There’s a real chance JD Vance doesn’t run for president at all.

🎬 **ROB LOWE SAYS HOLLYWOOD BLACKLISTED HIS MOVIE BECAUSE BEN SHAPIRO WROTE IT**
Rob Lowe made a movie with Nick Nolte and James Franco about a prisoner in Stalin’s Moscow. He says every film festival turned it down, and the only reason is who wrote the script.
He sounds a little shocked. Dude, welcome to the party.

But what would you do with a 10-minute head start before everything shuts off? Stay in the city or get out? 🤖 ONE STORY SAYS THE OUTAGES COULD ACTUALLY BE GOOD NEWS Josh Hawley says if this is all a coincidence, it’s the greatest coincidence in the history of the world. That’s what everybody is thinking. But the New York Post has a different take. Companies are using AI to hunt for holes in their own software, AI is finding a whole lot more than anybody expected, and the rush to fix them is what’s knocking things offline. We’re not telling you that’s the answer. It’s the first explanation that sounded plausible to both of us. | | | 🇺🇸 TRUMP IS FRUSTRATED WITH JD VANCE, AND IT’S GOING TO GET WORSE After the midterms, JD Vance said the Iran war is why Republicans lost. Trump agreed with him at first. Now he’s telling people Vance should have added that going in was the right call. Here’s the problem. JD doesn’t believe that, and he never has. So he’s got nowhere to go. And when somebody had to stand up this week and tell the country not to be scared about the outages, it wasn’t the vice president. It was Marco Rubio. Again. There’s a real chance JD Vance doesn’t run for president at all. 🎬 ROB LOWE SAYS HOLLYWOOD BLACKLISTED HIS MOVIE BECAUSE BEN SHAPIRO WROTE IT Rob Lowe made a movie with Nick Nolte and James Franco about a prisoner in Stalin’s Moscow. Peter, I hope you’re getting a chance to catch your breath and enjoy a quiet weekend after everything we poured into November. If you’ve lived in Virginia long enough, you already know there’s no such thing as an "off" year around here. While folks in other states get to tune out for a while, our next big test is already on the horizon, and I wanted to share a quick note on what the road ahead looks like for us. Next November, **every single one of the 140 seats in the Virginia General Assembly will be on the ballot at once.** Because we don’t have a race for Governor at the top of the ticket next year, there won’t be big statewide campaigns driving headlines and turnout. Holding onto our House majority and growing our razor-thin 21–19 Senate margin will come down to good old-fashioned, neighbor-to-neighbor organizing in our own communities. And just twelve months later, we roll straight into the 2028 presidential race. The local candidates we encourage to step up early, the voter lists we keep fresh, and the neighborhood precinct teams that stay connected during these quieter winter months are what will carry us through both 2027 and 2028. That’s where you come in, and I’m asking you to take one quick step with me this weekend: **plug into your local Democratic committee.** Our city and county committees are the heartbeat of everything we do across the Commonwealth, and they’re already gearing up for the fights ahead. Peter, When Democrats take back the House in January, we need to make Medicare for All a fight we win. But we can’t stop there—we need to close the gaps in our healthcare system that leave millions without access to care. We need to expand community health clinics, bring mental healthcare into schools, and make sure rural hospitals have the resources they need to serve their communities.

That's the kind of country I believe we can build, and the kind of government I'm fighting for in Congress—one that works for working people. ### Head Shaking Horizontally
---
**Meaning:** Indicates a swift shaking back-and-forth motion with the slight tilt to the left and the lines wrapped around the side of the emoji’s face.
**Evolution:** Perhaps the original intention for the emoji was positive or neutral, given the slight smile on the emoji’s face, but this icon is used almost universally for expressions of disapproval, disagreement, or disgust.
**Usage:**[Comment on a picture of a mushroom dish:] Nope 🙂↔️nope 🙂↔️nope 🙂 More 4 u cause u won’t catch me eating 🍄

name: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez
subject: Will it be easy? No.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez for Congress
body:
Is it possible? Yes...
#
See the guy at the microphone?
[](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-26-q4.h3BeQC&refcode=em20261123-12507-P_FND_EXP_MIS&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=3&akid=12507%2E2526796%2E1QPUQr)
He introduced me during our Fight Oligarchy event in Missoula, Montana shortly after Donald Trump was re-elected. He told the crowd he was a union man, a wildland firefighter, and the son of a public school teacher.
We didn't know what was going to happen then. We were just a couple of folks getting together, talking about the issues of the day.
But as it turns out, the momentum and the faith of coming together, organizing and refusing to give up created a window, and that man decided to raise his hand and put his hat in the ring to run for Congress.
His name is Sam Forstag, and two weeks ago he won his race in Montana -- one of the many great victories that made our huge Democratic majorities possible.
I share his story just to demonstrate what is possible when ordinary folks step up and try to accomplish something extraordinary.
All across the country there are millions of people like Sam who know what it's like to have your future and your life shaped by money, or by not having enough of it. Who know what it's like to work a thousand hours of overtime and still not have enough at the end of the month. Who know what it's like to dream big dreams of starting a business but looking at their student debt and realizing you couldn't afford it.
That was the same story I experienced.
But you don't have to run for office like Sam or I did (although you can and should). Every phone call, every door knocked, every social media post shared with friends and colleagues, every time you remind someone to vote, every donation made to make a difference is an extraordinary act.
That is what we did in November.
That is what I intend to do with this new Congress. To push the Democratic Party's agenda in a more progressive direction. Not just to say NO to Donald Trump, but to say YES we want wages to be higher; YES we want our water to be clean; YES we want to be able to work one job and have it afford a living and support kids; YES we want an affordable home, to go on vacation and keep something in our pockets.
Electing people like Sam Forstag is not the final destination. It was a necessary precondition to creating that kind of change.
Will it be easy? No, it will not.
Is it possible? Yes. But we will have to fight just as hard as we did to win the last election.
That is what I will be doing. But I cannot do it alone:
[Please make a contribution of any amount you can afford to help fund my work fighting for an agenda that works for all Americans and not just the one percent. We'll be organizing, holding events, building our communications channels and more. But I need your help to get it done. ](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-26-q4.h3BeQC&refcode=em20261123-12507-P_FND_EXP_MIS&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=4&akid=12507%2E2526796%2E1QPUQr)

In solidarity,
Alexandria
**[Contribute Now](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/14659?c0=aoc-email-26-q4.h3BeQC&refcode=em20261123-12507-P_FND_EXP_MIS&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=24&akid=12507%2E2526796%2E1QPUQr)**

name: Chris Westfall
subject: The House is next. Tell your Representative: protect wildlife.
body:
BAAJA is headed for a House vote. Urge your Representative to reject this assault on the Endangered Species Act!
BAAJA is headed for a House vote. Urge your Representative to reject this assault on the Endangered Species Act!
| [](https://support.defenders.org/s/6344805/38SyG9Xl)
---
[](https://support.defenders.org/s/6344806/38SyG9Xl)
---
| | |
---
#
|
---
[SIGN NOW: Tell the House to Keep Threatened and Endangered Animals Protected!](https://support.defenders.org/s/6344807/38SyG9Xl)
---
| | |
---
#
Defender,
#
**The House is about to decide the fate of America’s imperiled wildlife, and your voice is needed right now!**
#
[**Will your Representative defend the Endangered Species Act, or help bulldoze it?**](https://support.defenders.org/s/6344808/38SyG9Xl) If we don’t speak up now, wolves, grizzly bears, sea turtles and countless other imperiled species could pay the price.
#
The Senate has now passed the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026 (BAAJA), and it is headed to the House. Don’t let the name fool you: this bill is one of the most damaging attacks on wildlife we have ever seen. **If it becomes law, it will rewrite the ESA, our country’s strongest tool for protecting wildlife and preventing extinction, in profound and dangerous ways.**
#
**Here’s the good news: the House can still stop this. Your Representative can vote NO on final passage of BAAJA.**
#
[**The House vote could come at any moment, so there is no time to lose! Send an urgent message now and call on your Representative to protect endangered wildlife by voting NO.**](https://support.defenders.org/s/6344809/38SyG9Xl)
#
|
---
[TELL YOUR REPRESENTATIVE: VOTE NO!](https://support.defenders.org/s/6344810/38SyG9Xl)
---
| | |
---
#
**What makes BAAJA so dangerous? Plenty.**
#
* It will **cut federal wildlife scientists out of decisions** about projects that threaten endangered animals, removing a critical safeguard against extinction.
* It will **leave endangered animals extremely vulnerable** by shifting conservation responsibilities to underfunded, understaffed state agencies.
* It will **weaken protections across the country** by gutting the national system for protecting endangered species, replacing it with a patchwork of **_up to 50 different state processes,_** leaving wildlife with dangerously inconsistent protections.
* It will completely **exempt some highway and water projects from endangered species requirements** and never even ask the question whether the project might jeopardize the existence of threatened or endangered species-- effectively creating two **God Squads without the squad!**

#
**Worse still, Congress is racing to push these sweeping changes through in a lame-duck session, before newly elected members even take their seats and have a say.**
#
|
---
[TELL YOUR REPRESENTATIVE: VOTE NO!](https://support.defenders.org/s/6344811/38SyG9Xl)
---
| | |
---
#
The evidence is clear: the ESA is not the roadblock to development that its opponents claim it is. BAAJA would weaken core wildlife protections while ignoring the real problems that slow projects down.
#
The ESA has saved more than 99% of listed species from extinction. We can’t let a rushed vote tear it down.
#
[**Your Representative can still choose wildlife over this rushed bill. Make sure they hear from YOU today: tell them to vote NO on BAAJA.**](https://support.defenders.org/s/6344812/38SyG9Xl)
#
Thank you for standing up for threatened and endangered animals.
#
Sincerely,
#
|
---
|
---
| **Chris Westfall** Sr. Government Relations Legislative Counsel
Defenders of Wildlife
---
|
---
| [](http://www.facebook.com/DefendersofWildlife) [](http://twitter.com/defenders) [](https://www.instagram.com/defendersofwildlife/?hl=en) [](http://www.youtube.com/defendersofwildlife) [](https://www.tiktok.com/@defendersofwildlife)

disclaimer_text: Paid for by Swing Left, [swingleft
body:
Democrats’ greatest advantage over Republicans is our grassroots.
#
Hi there,
We just won a blue tsunami. So why are Democrats about to stop talking to the voters who made it all possible?
As our newly elected leaders prepare to assume their posts in Washington, campaigns across the country are shutting down. Staffers are packing up. Volunteers are heading home. And the conversations that helped power these wins are coming to an end.
We think this is backward.
That’s the case Swing Left Executive Director Yasmin Radjy makes in her latest op-ed to the Democratic ecosystem, now available on Substack:
[](https://act.swingleft.org/go/3333?t=1&akid=3474%2E1562180%2E_lrS1k)
[**Click here to read Yasmin’s op-ed, and share it with your networks.**](https://act.swingleft.org/go/3333?t=2&akid=3474%2E1562180%2E_lrS1k)
**[Read Now »](https://act.swingleft.org/go/3333?t=3&akid=3474%2E1562180%2E_lrS1k)**
Yasmin writes about one thing political leaders and voters agree on: Democrats need to deliver.
Winning voters' support once isn't the same as earning their lasting trust. On November 3rd, a whole new set of voters took a chance on Democrats, including in places that haven’t voted blue in generations.
We won’t be able to keep winning without these voters. But voter trust can crumble the moment Democrats stop listening.
That’s why Yasmin argues that volunteers like you, who just pulled off a blue wave, are the party’s greatest advantage. And we’re ready to keep going.
The work to win in 2028 and beyond begins now. That means making sure the volunteers who helped win tough races across the country can keep working in those districts—and keep listening.
Thank you for showing up this year, and thank you for reading!
— The Swing Left Team

**Since 2017, Swing Left has channeled the energy of grassroots volunteers and donors to elect Democrats, up and down the ballot, focusing on the most competitive races that can swing the national balance of power.** [**If you’d like to help support our work, you can make a donation using this link.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_sl_footer?refcode=em20261123-1&t=4&refcode2=3474_1562180__lrS1k&akid=3474%2E1562180%2E_lrS1k)

## Foxx Concedes after Recount
Republican Rep. Virginia Foxx [conceded](https://email.editor.flyovernorthcarolina.com/c/eJykkL_upCAUhZ8GOg1_BLSg2MZutt3SIF7GmyAYIDrz9hs32Sf4Vac4yZfznT-v5eUwYnr_dgfYkPyS4K4RWoOyhPz5-Jw8bFD3XE9sLtbVle8imNAd552Qy1lyPcG3hdPNGiP1tFGw3ExqkIKZke7WMICwqRCGcQKvmVfSaanWlfNRajVQtA-QcyE5Z0aNPddMT0NQXIxSKe7IwGDDlksf4jdfUFIubfeu5IjJ9T4fNNq9tbMS-YuImYj5vu_-Li4-JRHzo_WE9-7EliMR84XljQld93h2_0W7lC84Vijds4mImRa7nTfGiFUbMrD34fAflbafHnZZ8TcAAP__1ECA4w) the 5th Congressional District to Democrat Chuck Hubbard on Sunday, giving Democrats 11 of North Carolina's 14 U.S. House seats. Hubbard finished [330 votes ahead](https://email.editor.flyovernorthcarolina.com/c/eJykkLGu4yAURL8Gd0RwAeMUFNu4e9tuaRG4tq9EwAI2zvv7lZ-UL9hyNNLRnPnztXx5SpS33_6Jbs1hyXi2hL1jXdbyfoeSA0Zse2kHdZ_aw9fvBQSMXEoOajlqaQeGvsghOmvVeI8DOmnvRisQdhp2F7XCEA0EpR-PEdD4iCNELUxAM2kzkLuAUoKSUlgz3eQoxrtejYRJGSM90wIj9VJva_ouL6y51L4HX0ui7G-hPIfk9t6PxtQvBjOD-TzP2_kmknDVDGZfO4WEDOYX1Y0yeX4J8o8hrxjK39z5D5t_4NxcoeStYmtUsk88UuuVQmcwW22E1FYP1cXjpJSojZZpsT09pZ9d_X9ffTn4FwAA__8r_47-) after a recount in which Foxx gained just one vote. Foxx said she called Hubbard to congratulate him and called the peaceful transition of office "one of the true hallmarks of our system of government." Foxx, [first elected in 2004](https://email.editor.flyovernorthcarolina.com/c/eJykkM9uozAchJ_G3ILwz9iGgw_JatHuJkTRqlLVE_I_glUHI9sJydtX9BV6m8NoRt_33g-9dN7N17O8WTHOepjtmrzN2cZhDM-nDrO2xqYppMVl6ZOS8TVABWyH8Q7IsMSQFqvzgAsjOCesNYUVmLe0JlDxppgEtNK0FJTCBJOKG0YaXAPXtFWGW0ULJ7ZBjIFgXHHalJhVrK1HiqEhlGKJ6soal0MsR_8KDxvnEPOkZQzezbLU4VZ4MeW8JET2CDoE3bqu5ZpUlMaFrYCg29AQdEvwLju9RT3d9eduuislo0HQ0cvp0p_pr8MHe_tzPP3eH_jf_b_6-L9H0BVRmGV13rvEOKqr6006__2df2ruIeArAAD__-x1gWQ), chairs the House Rules Committee. Hubbard is a longtime journalist who got his start at a local newspaper owned by his family. Hubbard's win was Democrats' [seventh congressional flip](https://email.editor.flyovernorthcarolina.com/c/eJykkLuO5CAQRb8GZ7QMGD8Cgk2c9aYbWmUo2yXRYEFtP_5-5JHmCyY7UpWu7rn_7ssdKFLa_8ID3Zb8kvBVIzJjWbb8fvucPAasR64nMcS6QvksutW9VEpqs5wl1xM9L6oJbhhMP4UGnRom2xndDmNzOL-Nqgc9TbqbtFV2srCCCQB2w25dTUPuClRKG6XawY431bf91G1W6dFYq0B0LQbiXG5b_OQnlpQLHx5KjpTg5vOjie5gPqswf4SehZ73gpjqmkvmoyCE60no-dITej5zJCZ_IUb0TDldfBnLH2XJWR7_1xVKkJSk5eM67QVrpZwgykCVC3mWBTwKPTfFhfNFMVLtB9G1-wMofpfj3077dPorAAD__0wYkck) in North Carolina this year.
## Gas Tax Set To Return Dec. 1
North Carolina's 41-cent-per-gallon gas tax is [set to return](https://email.editor.flyovernorthcarolina.com/c/eJykkLFuwyAYhJ8Gb0T8YMAZGLp4S9eOFoHfMRI2FvxNnLevXKlP0PF0-u5093Wbbj7ltD0-_Ypu3sK04atlJMI6zeU4QtkCRmxLaXsin9vd1_ckhTQcgEs17bW0HQNN0EVnrTLX2KEDe9W9ksIO3eKi6dGinVEoo6XyGKMZgtHzXYMKFrrkzkAAqQCE1cMFjDDXftYgB6U1eNYLjIlKvcz5XZ5Yt1JpCb6WnDZ_CWXtsluI9sbUB5Mjk-MrUAJ5WkyO5ygmx1yCz6c8af6H84dvnPzBU-MNiVPhFdv3ijxiwPWOlUNXXdxfKefUjGW9eKw-5d9e-u9rTyd_AgAA__9irYLt) Dec. 1, when a temporary suspension expires. The pause [took effect Oct. 10](https://email.editor.flyovernorthcarolina.com/c/eJyk0LGO4yAYBOCnwR0W_NgQFxTXuMu1V1q_8e8YHQEL2JC8_SqR9gm2Humb0fy7Llf0wcfbX7yT3aNbIrUSqFbKy56eT5eio43KkcrpK4ayYn4tIEBzKTmo5cypnOTqIrvNGqP0tHVkpZnGQYEwl-6waIw2ckU3oZpI0jq6YRJIWu8CUI2dt29QSlBSCjNeeqmFnoZ9lHBR4yiRDYI2X1Pu9_BKD8ox5Xo4zCn4iL1L9y7Yo9azMPWHwcxgbq31ba2Pd8hgfhcwmKVgMIuJwfwR-A_B07575zGEFy9f5aS4FT5I7ihWfsPCKz55O7Dy_zE1BnOX7XY2H4Iv2rBB3O7ow2dI_e2NDwvfAQAA__8i4Ic4). At 41 cents, this year's rate is the highest in state history. Senate leader Phil Berger, R-Rockingham, [said he sees](https://email.editor.flyovernorthcarolina.com/c/eJykkLGOpDAQRL_GZI1wgzETOLiEbC-9EPWYBix5bMv2Duzfn5hf2PiVSvXq39fyRc67sP-lF5st2CXwWTzXynnZ4nXZGCyvXI5Ykqvky5Pyz4IdjiAlYL-kHEtiWxfZrEbrfnysDRupH2rosdNTc5ip2xTR8GSLz03ZTY-oVK9JI8oR5dA4cxdKib2UnVZTK8dufAybkjj1SkkSQ8erqzG3m_-Jb84h5npYytG7QK2Nr8abo9ZURP9H4CxwPs-zPTP5Gwqcby2Bs4-W_E1dPWCnApUuKN8lcSguBihcoUbgK7nMEOwnk7KzXMDGb79CdoWhVMrVhR1WtiAhxDfcBgLnJps1nc57V0Ythm5_kftsaOpv730b_B8AAP__SweRGw) "no reason" to extend the break. ## Blue Ridge Parkway Fully Reopens
The National Park Service [reopened](https://email.editor.flyovernorthcarolina.com/c/eJykkLGupSAURb9GOwwHEbSgmMbuTTulOcJRySAY4D6vfz-58wuv3tkrK-vP1_KFPvi4_8aTzBbtEukugWqlvGzp_bYpWnJUjlQuXzGUFfOzCC4UA2CiX66cykW2LtA6o3WvJteSAT0Nshdcj-1hrBoBHI5Wk1RaEIyrVrgq0Q_bRFy23nyAAKIH4HoYO1BcTXIbQIz9MAA2kpPzNeVuC0_6phxTrofFnIKP2Nl0tsEctV6l6X81Ym7EfN93d7-9B_GZGzFjrt4GasS8hhex7N1O7ML898aHba8QHpYpXRQLO145e4uR2EGBIjGHJ-6fq5YDB1CyzcZdtw_BF6UbyfcTffjvUX9a8duIfwEAAP__Z4eH8w) the last section of the Blue Ridge Parkway damaged by Hurricane Helene this weekend, restoring the full scenic route. ## Student Turns Himself In over APSU Noose
A male student [turned himself in to Austin Peay State University police](https://email.editor.thetennesseeflyover.com/c/eJykkL3OozAQAJ_GdI78Q0goXFxD9117JVrsdVh9jo3sBcQ9_Sn3Cl8_Go3mz9f8BZQov37DGx1znDOeLSEz1vlvKVyBMmVPATPzXr_xivWajTKD1FoaO4NnOnDuoQtuMXqE3nfo9GO899Zo_exW9zDWWB_GASMoHB8RoV9MHAPcFz_0oSP3EWptrNbqae83-4yogrJaL0O8Ky16hYG41BuvyJgztoYY01UOrDdf3l1yK_PWhP0lzCTM5BPU73ZQSpjL-UGEmVLxkISZNqytZHmuRa57fsm2FkzgUeZSGkrea8YgKUtgCXtjynJDuGRjYJR7pgNrI76EmbrqwnZSStSGh-jV6w2U_hfxD3cezvwLAAD__7_Kjuk) after a noose made from a shoelace was found Friday hanging from a tree near Harvill Hall, a freshman dorm. Police determined the act [wasn't motivated by racial hatred](https://email.editor.thetennesseeflyover.com/c/eJykkLGu4yAURL8Gd1hcjB27oNjG3dt2S4sHFxsFQwQ3RtmvXyXF_sDrRhrpzOj8-dq-TIgh7b_NiZrIbwlbjUiEZfubMxUTUkg2OExEz3LHly-vTQo5cQAuh81YChduynROf0tYjLIdargtoxokwNwdWs5uFHaalQUFYrk55RDRLxbGcVbOd0G_gQByABDzMPbD7FE4MQB8T34UwJRAFyiXng4kTAlrRfTxlS8svc1nF_VB9Khs-MXkyuTaWutbPa93yeT65jO5Anwyk2vKuSL3-ZkcP0zaQ9o5FURuc4y4I7fmfDwrP4NzEfn_TX5gwcrbYYg35PeUG5NrV7R7tBBjqNONKbGfJsTPL_qh1EvLfwEAAP__DgSNKQ) and found no ongoing threat, and the case has been referred to Student Affairs. Students gathered near the dorm to protest, and some say they [want more transparency about the investigation](https://email.editor.thetennesseeflyover.com/c/eJykkLHOnDAQhJ_GdEbeNXD8hYs0dH_alMiY9Z11xkb2Aro8fUSUN0i5O5rRfPPre_62IYb0_Gk3Msx-TnTVSMxU5t85c7EhheTCSon5KG_6-PKZUeEgASTq2ToOJ82dbVazIHzZzjVk4PHVdxoBxuZlrAa_YN-NdvEwOOj8Yt2inH4goCfXBHMHAqAGUKPuWz16UqvSAMvgewWiU7QGzqXlFzGlRLUS-fjJJ5XW5a2J5sW8V6F_CJwETtd1tde7pFsUON1UAqeYnY3y3-GiLe96hhhJ4FToJslJWs9UZMq5kvT5SKu8n3s9pLPbftzOpph1v0KMoQ4P0annZkP8W4P_c8PT4J8AAAD__-BJiYs) and what consequences the student could face. The university said a noose "carries a painful history" and that it will ensure accountability through campus processes and with local law enforcement.

A child [fell from the Wilderness Express train ride](https://email.editor.thetennesseeflyover.com/c/eJykkLGu4yAQRb8Gd0QM2I5dUGzj7m27pUVgiEePQASztpKvXzn7Ca8b6YyOrs6fr_XLUaJ8_-0eaJnjmvFoCZmxru9SuDrKlD0FzMx_6ze-Yn2tWulRAkhtVueZdlx71wV70zC73ndo4ToPvdEAU7fZeBu1mlXsx9GbaYozoNNhmLW7Djh635E9hQDaAKjJDBczRVRBGYDbGAcFolcYiEu98IaMOWNriDG9yo714sujS3ZjfjZhfgm9CL0cx3E52mM_odDL6Rd6AfjcJyc-JfKbQpOVAsrs2rZTSijfpch7YVmeWB2X2qRjxsxUsmxcnv__XWSs0m-UgowupSY_sYReumrD86CUqI1X0av7w1H6rOQfJt6t_hcAAP__S9GS3Q) at the Nashville Zoo Friday afternoon and was struck by the train, suffering bruises and scrapes that weren't considered serious. A witness said other children on the ride got the operator's attention, and the train stopped immediately. It's the first serious incident in the ride's more than 20-year history. The zoo, located at the historic [Grassmere farm](https://email.editor.thetennesseeflyover.com/c/eJyk0DuO2zAQgOHTSJ0FvvQqWKRRKrsNkIYYiUNrYIo0yIkM5_QL7xW2_Juv-P9c3RUoUrrf4EDLHFzCV43IjMX9z5kLUKK0kcfE_K888B3K2ymhhouUF6UdbEwnOgOtt6uSM5itRSvHuTdaSTm1ux1n7yWYPsDk12kOKoAxAb1W47BO3rRkP6CUSkspJt13egoovNBSrkPohWyMQE-cS8c7MqaEtSKG-M4nlm7LRxvtzvysjf7VqKVRC6buRQ96oifocrk3avl0o5Yb1P2kGNH9zdkBu98Faj2wYFusf74oRqrD2BhxP4Dit84_XHNa9RUAAP__NNx7KA) in South Nashville, draws about 1 million visitors a year.

The [617-foot AT&T Building](https://email.editor.thetennesseeflyover.com/c/eJykkL3O4jAQAJ_G6Yi86_wWLrgiHVRIV1pOvElWGAc5SxD39Ce-V_jKaWak-XtxF8-R03L1D7Iis0v03iOJUHb_tk2y58Rp4kBJ5JXv9Jnzx6HG5gRwQuP8JHyQq3wR7IjQ-2oqyELb15VBgK5YbTs2Vd_qbqzrsTO9Ie0DzrodMfgReizYfoUAaAB0Z-rSdDPpoA3A2My1BlVpCixbLmUloZRo34nm-NkOyuW0PYpoV5HnrsxZ4aBwoFS--c5PCuzLLS8Khy8rHM43hTU2N_fnxTFwWpzC7ur39eAYSWFfZBueb46R96ZVlV4enuNPRH556LD4PwAA__-vW3pq), nicknamed for its two spires that resemble Batman's mask, opened in 1994. ## Delta Glitch Snarls Holiday Travel
A failure in Delta Air Lines' weight-and-balance system [triggered a ground stop](https://email.editor.thegeorgiaflyover.com/c/eJykkT1u3DAUhE9DdVzwb6V1oWJhr5pEzk8TuBKeqUeKMZcUyGcJe_tAvkLqGczgm_kzTiOEGJJ_hTv25N2UcK8RibBMM0YCHwPZhRZIH9WHLSRv86SEarmUXOkJLIUNJwPN3GsxozSXBnvZPZ2NVqq9NEsvpTFGS3exM4gnDcrpzjnRnltpnJVtE_ojUEqlpZRSdKfDABd8l0Z0VgvBjMA5UC4nWtBjLj6Ai4-8YTnZfG9ivxCtlekrUwNTw77vp72-03aoTA0HFFNDzBYiU4ON8KCcuM2fiR5MDb7kzzTzSnnl6Bxa4gsUqi5gnPlfsB81Jw4x8q9NOITCY0hYuYvBL1S5A-AF11zoKHpW19ef39Ttdr51319-j7_expfb-OP6_MbU0JR-XvcQY6htx4zwdwjxC4P-84GtV_8CAAD___CrnAs) for Atlanta-bound flights Sunday morning, days before the Thanksgiving travel rush. The FAA downgraded the stop to a ground delay shortly after 8:40 a.m. and said the problem was unrelated to air traffic systems. Hartsfield-Jackson still logged [364 delays Sunday morning](https://email.editor.thegeorgiaflyover.com/c/eJyk0L2O3DAMBOCnsTsZ-vFvoSKNu0ub0uBKtExElg4S1869fbCLFOmvJzjzza-P7QMoUgo_4UTLYd8S3jUiM5bNY2QIkdgdfED6XQNdlILLm5Z6FEoJbTZwTBduPbTeGulR9XOLVk3L0Butx7k9rHtIOYMbsJ_GxwDjoBaEZdnVPGnttGnJvh4qpY1SSsmp2820w4wP1cvJGSmbXqInzqXjAwPmEgj2-JUvLJ3LZxvtwfxZG_Oj0Wuj1_u-uz3_GYAjJIbXTaPXF63R65slgIqIlLAKeHI-gSknQbU-UXChELBUcTyTL-ir-J8vuMCFUXiM8FXFv4i2WP95U4xUx6npZTiB4rsbf3PWy-q_AQAA__-jZpDL), according to FlightAware. With the system down, Delta crews calculated loads by hand, which [limited gate space for arriving flights](https://email.editor.thegeorgiaflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOqzAQRb_GdCB7DIFXuHgNXbbdEk3swYzW4AhPQPn7FfmF7UY6o6N77_d9uiMn3uIXruQkztNGZ0kkQvsUKAnGxOIXWXD7KZEP3qLPE2i41cbUYCf0wgdNLVbBWR3ItENFzvT_utYC3IZqce1M2vpuwMF7mDuNtkPjQ6fpgXPoqGJ3CY0Ba4wxum9m28840MO0uvdWa9VqCix5b2ShSHmPjHN654P2xue1Sm4ReRZl_ysYFYzneTanZH9BBeNlVzAac92gYPw0qwu-S40vySsK563mUl5Uao-vwlusA6XrYfvAkwMpGKvdhefJKXG59arVcUVOnwjyx_UOB78BAAD__-O-hNk) as departures slowed. Delta later [said its automated systems were back online](https://email.editor.thegeorgiaflyover.com/c/eJykkT1u3DAUhE9DdVzwb6V1oWJhr5pEzk8TuBKeqUeKMZcUyGcJe_tAvkLqGczgm_kzTiOEGJJ_hTv25N2UcK8RibBMM0YCHwPZhRZIH9WHLSRv86SEarmUXOkJLIUNJwPN3GsxozSXBnvZPZ2NVqq9NEsvpTFGS3exM4gnDcrpzjnRnltpnJVtE_ojUEqlpZRSdKfDABd8l0Z0VgvBjMA5UC4nWtBjLj6Ai4-8YTnZfG9ivxCtlekrUwNTw77vp72-03aoTA0HFFNDzBYiU4ON8KCcuM2fiR5MDb7kzzTzSnnl6Bxa4gsUqi5gnPlfsB81Jw4x8q9NOITCY0hYuYvBL1S5A-AF11zoKHpW19ef39Ttdr51319-j7_expfb-OP6_MbU0JR-XvcQY6htx4zwdwjxC4P-84GtV_8CAAD___CrnAs) and that it was rebooking and refunding affected travelers.
## Georgians Feel Thanksgiving Pinch
A new survey estimates [42% of Georgians are struggling with hunger](https://email.editor.thegeorgiaflyover.com/c/eJykkLuO3SAQhp8Gd1jM4GtBkcbdSZvSwmaMUTAcATHK26-82mL77UaaX99_-fNaX9p5F-xvfZEq9lgD1eypFEqrIV-09a7sZzl1-Jutu12we1xR4MABOMpV78XdtHa6MUoKQ9BNDSkY576TiMPUnKqnHmEyG0jRi15u82b6fqdhkAN280yNUw8QACUAgBjbQ46HnmiDToy7FIJ1gowrMbXlJEsxWacP_z_elNo9Xo1XZynvzOQvhgvDpdba1mTq82S4PHSGC8BzI8Plex1-xGh41bkQf1PKLpfML-e9iyHzL7OQ-aF34ue_YCkxXJqkzLs-qjyMrBP20s5_Zik_nPFW-BEAAP__NWOG8Q) as families head into a pricier Thanksgiving. ## Judge Blocks Memorial Circle Arch
A federal judge in Alexandria [blocked construction](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkLFuhDAQRL8GujutFxubwkWa6y5tSrTYa1jFBydjgfL3EfmFNCONRprRvK_n-CTJss6f9GJfjzSufO6Za-UyUgnLlLfwzTFJ4bls505rPJcRAfubUjfsRgpVDh41tdEn0kxDy17ZwegOO2PaxTvF3cBKc3RkKACiGXroU2ALCZ1pxV99SmGnLtF3bQEM26RVCi7q2GjgKHUr97rwIWWWVSjln-3gcg_bq81-qfW9N91Hg48GH_S-blzRZUqVkLnBR7LTMAGBdqCdMmCgcxHATgkthDi0xcf3KTnL3ttGw_wiyX8D9Z9sDo-_AQAA__8HXnYg) of President Trump's proposed 250-foot arch at Memorial Circle in a lawsuit brought by Arlington County. The order has no set expiration date, according to the plaintiffs' lawyers. U.S. District Judge Leonie Brinkema [issued the order Friday](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkLGunTAMhp8GtiASAlyGDF3YbteOyI0dcBuSqySH6L59lfMKXX5ZsmT_3_fr8_gE9hzOn3CTKY87AtXsqRRKByR7_fbR_iV0nOhMsWYIWK9DjWoRUgo1HWALP3Ro6NE40ARbT0au26wnNc1zfxkEt7lxk7i6DXEENeLqlo9lc27B2U49m3ZPSjXJFnrQ6zjOtDotnf1AjZ0eCbnENJSLHk4nBwbnv-NDabDx7r25SvnK3fSjU3un9lrrAMmHWNu6U3t70Kldyja3-PPCk8SbLoub7pgYvLCcrCfRwAUHAampKTEIG1-hfGfhoeYXF1G5XCJEQQEFQiGRqXRq75PBr8rec17WTo_nDezfDct_yn2M-hcAAP__amqQnw), two days after a D.C. judge extended a separate construction ban through Dec. 3. Brinkema's order keeps construction on hold while Arlington's case proceeds. Arlington County argues the arch could worsen traffic and threaten public safety. The administration [says it will appeal](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkD2StCAQQE-DGRZ_6mdA8CVms-mGFgON9g6CBag1t99yrrBJ14u6-73vx_wwGDAuX2YDXU8_R7hKgFohzybb9RmSfYHzmGHJ6SomumudBRM95ZwKORtb8YRZmcZpbxSYsQHNh7FTUsiua1Y9St91vXRPJlVvlRhBeGkVOMlG23nWoL73cS4kv4dq1cBYB4NX3Nt_TjmiGDisKbd1hRPzghGND-90Qm5t2pqg11r3QuR_IiYipuu62tf-LG3KCxHT7UTEtKeAFe2N90EiJs4_TMRkaAGboqM_h1uAfrQLrfnY9kLvELSYN8aFYi30iAFfEN60JloOawEcxUhtOnJtsnb7hSFg6Qei2LIZDJ8n6x_7nlr8BgAA___5eJDS) and contends a 1925 law authorizes the project.

The latest [Forest Service update](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkD2unTAUhFdjOhD-A27hIlJE99KmROfax-A8g5F9wMruI-4W0kwzoxl98_tr-YIQw7H-gh0N3X45sJaIRJgXyHZ7x2S_0fmQcc2pFjhc3RbRi6HlvBVyAUvhxkVB44wHhfBq0PDxpZUUUutmM_6t3loLP01uwBG97sWkECYBL6mB2yaYp49zIfkjqlNj32scveLeTk45pnp0gVLuaMM75DUcAXz8m27MnU17E81GdBYmfzAxMzHXWjtfuqs46NZ0MzHnfmJiXusfJmaImKk8sS0Qtgm-Wx-B2geyvU4HhB843oqByfmifSnpyhaZ_Gk3oPWkz2o27qwhxlCGkal-3SHEj0H_-eRtxL8AAAD__zv-iJQ) lists containment at 0%. ## Right Whale Calves Surface Off Virginia
Two endangered North Atlantic right whales were spotted with their newborn calves near the Chesapeake Bay shipping channel this week, and [officials are urging mariners to use caution](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkLFuxCAQRL8Gd1gGY_uuoEjj7tKmtNawGHQcWHhldH8fOUq-IM1Kqxk9zczXY3lAiCFtn_BCTadbEtYjIhGWBYrxa8zmidaFglvJ9YBkq19kJ0cuBJf9AobCiYuCxmoHCuHeoBbTfVC97Ieh8Xo0opdiEnbtHQ4SxXCzaKwdxW2cBiGaoC-eELIX11GtmrpuwMkp4czNKstUhzZQLi15PEPZQgrg4jufWFqTX03Unmg_WP_B5MzkXGttK5zvS2RyvjoxOcdsIPLf5w_DVwTjmZwxWUgbFrQ85UKeA0VIFAyvHiJyA9HxY89ElwOhcOPxgB3hiXyFN5NzU7Tda4gxHOPEVLe9IMSfgPTPbU8tvwMAAP__SxKRYQ). Researchers [filmed 15-year-old Snail and her calf by drone](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkLFu7CAQRb8Gd1iA8Xq3oHiNu31tSmsWBjMKNqsxwcrfR84vpDm61T3S-XguT6BM-_ofNnS1xWXH88hYK_IC7NMrF_-JIRLjyuU8YA9nWowyN6m1NMMCvlLDxUIXXASL8OjQ6ekx2sEM49gld4s2GIWP4T6MRvtJKXxhRAMwQoBgO3LXn9Zm0BdsbyelRpyi1dHfgw3CKgxUC_c1YSNeaSeI-bs05N6Xrcsu1fo-xPBPmFmYuSb0X8y41xX6wqsw86UQZtb62hcaBSyHrGeRW2GUTGuq8kyQUXrIDQ_J6AsHDMLMHbvwPilnOm6TsGrdgPKvu_4xW3PmJwAA__-UUoJJ) Thursday, then found 34-year-old Calvin with her fifth known calf off Cape Henry on Friday. Gib Brogan of Oceana called the bay's mouth, busy with Navy traffic and ships bound for Baltimore, "extremely risky." NOAA estimates about 380 right whales remain, and vessel strikes are a major cause of injury and death. Federal guidance asks mariners to [slow down where right whales are likely](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkDtuxCAUAE-DO1v8vLYLijTuNm1K6y08zFNYWAEyyu2jzRXSTDkjzdf9uANFSucnPNG0yx8Je43YGpYDig2PmO03Ok8Fz5J7heR6OCSXt1GIUaoDbKMLDw2DMx40wjagEcs2ayXVPA_BIIdNu3nzq7RS3ezKHXfIVxAPpRQ-BjJvnxBSiTf0pBfOZ1y8Ft6uTjumOTpquUwt4EXlpETg40--sEw2P4doQmuvytQHkzuTe-998lQDFsI6pQwwnflicq8vtISVyT3l0sIILUJqZMdCZ2hjDxBxKMa9OsVI9bYwzc8nUPzLtH8euoz8DQAA__83fH0l). Most right whale calves are born off Florida and Georgia, hundreds of miles south. Survey teams [recorded a newborn off Virginia Beach in December 2024](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkDGupDAQRE9jMhBuzDAEDjYhm003RI3dxq019sj2gub2K770T_CTCkqqetL781pfyIHj_hsP0vV0a6SrBKqV8orZ-C0k85es40x7TlfBaC-_Qg-PVsoWhhVN5ZNWhY3VDhXh3JCW0zyqAYZxbLx24Fw_biTh-TD9bOUm5WzMTCCNVUgN6_tPShjkHapTU9-PNDklnXlaZYXqyXJNuaueTs47R0YXPumk3Jl0NEH7Wt9FDL8ELAKWiOfnwMyRypsMUzlSvPcc9-5fEbBsIe0Clsy7r-3lMVBrMLi23AXZ9hsiYGmytu-LQ-DymITq9wM5fFHrD4WdGv4HAAD__2yCg0k), the earliest documented calf sighting in Virginia waters.

## Dayton Philharmonic Musicians Strike
Dayton Philharmonic musicians [called a strike](https://email.editor.theohioflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGOszAMwPGngQ0Um0DLkOFb2PqtN6I0MY11gaDEV9S3P3GV7gVu-0uWLP_8cZtvliNvj_92JSMpLPNGR4kkQnn29iVpW78KO7ZbKZL5kwJxmVHh0AA02M17TmUnJzPU3mjqYBlrMnAZe91hj1gH02s9-CvC4JxCZ_WovL8O96sG9INWS83mXAiAHQD0iK0DINLWjqq_e4tjpRV5lpRbCZQCpyW-0pNy69JaRxNE9lJ1_yqcKpyO42hfNqR0TiucTlGF054iC7szbRZ2kc58G5s9cAw2r2lj1_yKmze5wQ5RdWOPbZA11tn4_eAYuQyXSqvHajn-XCJ_fuHT4HcAAAD__2_2iJ8) Saturday after contract talks broke down over how many rehearsals and concerts the orchestra would guarantee. Principal clarinetist John Kurokawa said management cut the maximum guarantee from 119 rehearsals and concerts to 70, resulting in a 28% pay cut. A later offer raised the guarantee to 75. The walkout could affect Dayton Ballet’s [December performances](https://email.editor.theohioflyover.com/c/eJykkLEO2yAURb8Gb0Tmge14YOjiLV07WgSew1MwWPCcKH9fpZX6A52vdHTP-XVbb44S5cdPt6PlErc147slZMa6BvfhkvezkSeXW-NKT4xIbYUeRqmUBL0etbQDPa-qC9agVtvcoVXTPBgNA0AXLQSt-3ncrlPwgxvNCCFcr2abZw39ZFxH9gtUCrRSagC4eKUQjXNzP9yDg1mYHgNxqReOWCKVLX3KC-vFl71LNjIfTegfAhYBSywlJMr4HQUsX7SARSkBy18jeURK0dW9ZPLyn598u_SU5WR5nMyUH5Ijynyyr84_sUrKMpTzzgKWrtpwvCklauMkTP_YHaU_b_i_M74s_A4AAP__H2uJ8Q) of _The Nutcracker_ at the Schuster Center, scheduled for Dec. 11-13 and 18-20. The [Dayton Performing Arts Alliance](https://email.editor.theohioflyover.com/c/eJyk0L1ug0AQBOCngc6IXY6fK65I485pU6IFFljl4E53G1t--8jxI6Qe6dPMfN3GG4mXc_ukg52GfR1PfmTPqpzGhZ4azuMnyyx05qxJvnlnySPW2F0ALtiMMYUcedYRysUZbmC1JTvobWsabBHL3fFq-hV4omFoydi-7qyljgc23EzDBKW4FwiADQC0iNUMwGyIbN1OC6EtTM2LaEiV7hx2Cat_hjunag5H6d2uGnPRfBR4LfD6rh05rSEdcm6UNFchba8ohst7RoHXMrklPsR7yV1fmHo7SPyfqP--4u7wNwAA___AVnYj) said the two sides had already reached tentative agreements on several issues. Alliance President Patrick Nugent said meeting the musicians’ requests would take stronger ticket sales and more donations.
## Ohio’s Tom Jackson Dies at 75
Tom Jackson, the Cleveland native who helped the Denver Broncos reach their first Super Bowl and spent 29 years analyzing NFL games alongside Chris Berman at ESPN, [died at 75](https://email.editor.theohioflyover.com/c/eJyk0DtuxCAUheHV4A7LXPwsKNLQTdqUFo_rMRkMFtyMNbuPJltIfaRPR__Xbb2ZEEO6f5oDFeV9WxNeNSIRltWbF-V0_NTggkm1UgkP3DHUFToYuRAc5HqWXE90tIrGqx6l2JYGlZiWoZcwADS76jo7z35yOBoHxjor0Uo52mWbZ-wFNEG9QSFACiEGgNYJgdgbs3SD9QYW1nfoA-XS0o55D3mLr_zE0rp8NFHtRGdl8oOBZqCv62qxnuk9MtBpiwx0pVxeDPTKQAfPQA_dMIppmhloygf_Nu5Rc-K25ORy5ZVM4W-FR7xj8twHrHwamqL8eYUYQx0n1nf3w4T4d4P-3e-p4DcAAP__b2aGRA). # Edit & Select Text with this Hidden iPhone Feature
Did you know you can now use the keyboard on your iPhone like a trackpad? This hidden feature makes it easy to move your cursor around and select text on your iPhone. Let's go over how to control the cursor with the keyboard.
## Why You’ll Love This Tip
* **Position the cursor in the right spot with ease.**
* **Save time correcting spelling and grammatical mistakes in your message.**

## How to Move Cursor on Keyboard with Spacebar
### System Requirements
_This tip was performed on an iPhone 15 Pro running iOS 27. Find out how to update to the[latest version of iOS](https://click.iphonelife.com/ga/click/2-17209627-5-0-262141-8633192-4ae5088e6c-btdfdd21da)._Your iPhone's keyboard has a hidden trackpad feature that you can access just by tapping the space bar. To learn more about tricks to make using your iPhone easier, sign up for our free [Tip of the Day](https://click.iphonelife.com/ga/click/2-17209627-5-0-262141-8633193-3697b420d2-btdfdd21da) newsletter. Now, let's go over how to move cursor on iPhone keyboard:
1. Type in any area that you can, such as your Notes app, a URL bar, or a text message. For this example, I'll use the Notes app.

|
---
2. Tap and hold the space bar.

---
3. The keyboard will turn light gray. Swipe finger across the spacebar to move the cursor until you have it at the desired place in the text area, and then lift your finger to continue typing.

a hundred thousand individual grassroots supporters, not billionaires or
corporate PACs.

now. But, I

**Good Morning!** On this day in 1889, the world's first jukebox [made its debut](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDFuhDAQRU9jOhAeG3tduEhDt2lTogHG4I3BiJ2FcPtoc4XUX_pP733duzvGFNfpExfyHHK30vlMxEx7N1JiDClOM-cX40S8v5ZtwL2DGkwpZQmqw4HjQZ0sRh-IgFRBXlrXaKW0dsXs1c3R0PcOTI8AFGQwTqrREFpLxjZF9O87KUFJqWptKtuQ6TVgj9YFh4PQNY2R8149clx5ppCufNBeDXkpkp-Zt6dQHwJaAe15ntWFc87vVUD79hHQbniVW8KrjOtBK9NYPl7f1OefUjZ1I2_K6GrmJRW7H7czphSfxgpdTwvG9Afi_-U5PPwGAAD__9rkeko) at the Palais Royale Saloon in San Francisco. A nickel bought one song through a stethoscope-style listening tube, and the machine pulled in about $1,000 in its first six months. Thirty-six years after he booby-trapped the McCallister house, Macaulay Culkin is [coming back as Kevin](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL9utDAQxJ8GOiP_A47CxdfQ3demRItZwDljE7MG3dtHpEudcnd-Gs3Mx3N4gvMuLP9hQ0NzHAJeh0ciTMOEnmD2blkpZoIFKeVtt5AGyWXDhGBSDWDJnTiIcjIzokRVohFtV2ultO7K1TxQc3jorp45n2AW9cgt1k2nldSNaHXpzG0nhFRCKK6bqq2xGbWEEdpu7sAWmuPkKKbqM7pAK87-HU9MlY1b6c1KtB-F-lfIvpD9dV1VGO1d49YL2e9xZzZ7ygl_X-yGCtlvYCF7eN__lwvsQGIJKafAXni6wDZrwXt3ECa2xg0Z-BiQHfiV0bNkAzSC160uk5n2y91o0xaaLxs4_5OS_rbtaeR3AAAA__8S8pF7) in a new _Home Alone_ , this time as a dad. So tell us: What's your favorite Christmas movie? Vote in today's poll, and if we left it off the list, hit reply and let us know. Which diets actually work? Low-carb, keto, carnivore, the Mediterranean diet: they all promise results, but the research tells a different story, and some have almost no scientific evidence to back them up. The system that failed calculates how much each plane weighs and how that weight is distributed before takeoff. Crews switched to manual calculations, and nearly half of Delta's Atlanta departures were by early afternoon. It's the third aviation breakdown in nine days, after an FAA router failure grounded flights nationwide Nov. 13 and United lost its own weight-data system three days later. Tuesday and Wednesday are also expected to be the busiest outbound driving days of Thanksgiving week. The footage shows Revolutionary Guard commanders touring tunnels lined with missiles, some deliberately blurred, and a handwritten sign insulting the White House. Underground storage makes the weapons harder for U.S. and Israeli forces to find and destroy. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is pressing Trump to join a four- to seven-day bombing campaign, and Mossad's director flew to Washington two weeks ago with intelligence that Iran is and advancing its chemical weapons. Trump says he is in no rush to decide. Tehran has another front to watch today. Armenia is launching the "Trump Route," a U.S.-backed transit corridor along Iran's northern border, after a senior Iranian adviser warned Tehran would "" if Trump and his allies crossed its red line. Culkin Returns for Home Alone Sequel Macaulay Culkin will play Kevin McCallister again in a new Home Alone film now in at Disney, 36 years after the original. Seth Rogen and Evan Goldberg will write and produce. Culkin, now 46, pitched the idea to studio executives after years of declining to return. He previously described a possible sequel in which a grown Kevin, now a father, must navigate traps set by his own son. The new film's plot hasn't been announced. The 1990 original cost about $18 million and took in $285.8 million domestically, making it one of the of its era. Culkin returned for Lost in New York in 1992, then sat out four more installments. Disney declined to comment, and there is no release date or casting beyond Culkin. Rogen and Goldberg a Muppets special for the studio. ## Cruz, Talarico Unite for Space Academy
Sen. Ted Cruz said he and Sen.-elect James Talarico, the Democrat who beat Ken Paxton this month, agreed in [a half-hour phone call](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0L1uwyAUxfGnwRsR90KMGRi6eEvXjhbG1wEJG8u-zUefvkrUN-h8pL_0O1-X4RJyyev1Myzk-THXYaX7UYiZ9mHLHFNer5zo2EKkEMNEyzPWARW2EkCiHkLkfKMBmsmPanLQkAfrzkafEaBJHowCHEmbTrtZOz3G0Rki2ykLk-2oyf5VA0ANqBTAyaGNcdbKQQSru1YYRVPmup84EdMjHHN51hvtp1iXpvjEvB1CfwjsBfacKOVSXpvAPtWFXiKB_UFrYBLYt6jPWhkZ9-8fyaGEPccq32H5dso_qMC-2f203XMp-WitMOq6hPxuN_zPu24efwMAAP__X3p-hA) Friday to jointly push for President Trump's proposed U.S. Space Academy in Houston. Cruz said Saturday that [a bipartisan push](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGSozAMxvGngc6MJWOMCxfXpMu1VzKOLIJvTWBAG5J9-p1k9g221_w1v-_feTjHXPLt-jfOHOQxLsONj72wCG_DmoWmfLvKxPsaiSPFxPOTlgE1dgpAoRkiSb7zAHUKF5081BzAedsaiwD1FC5GM1GrTe9tPzrb2S5Zh54T-X7UVOfwqgGgAdQaoPHoiEajPRA403dVqzllWbZGJhZ-xH0sz-XOW0PLXJcwiax7Zf5UeKrwdBxH8zIczB-vgwpPwknR9vml_seZdyWxxC3ToiiWot5B9fapH6ACdBY729ZbSOuRS8l756pWX-eYy_ur_HKse8DvAAAA__8x436_) would make Texas' bid "really powerful." The state faces 24 other contenders, including Florida and Ohio, and a presidential commission will send its recommendation to Trump on Dec. 26. Texas [pitched Houston to NASA](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0L2OqzAQBeCnMZ2RZ8xv4eI2dLntlsjYQ7DWYISHkLz9KtG-wdajOUff-bqNNxti2O7_7UqGn3MaN7pyJGY6xj2wW8J254Xybh1ZZz2tL5dGVNhIAIl6tI7Dg0YovJmU76EgA21fV7pGgGIxpG03T53tsPNVP1k_977ttELsoW6oLoJ5pwGgBlQKoOyxdW7WqgcHre4aUSnygdNR8kJMT5vn-EoPOkqX1iKahXnPQv8TOAgcrusqv592ex8FDm-OwOHzJnBY0pk5bdKlM3o5kZxPPg-SS1pJplmeWX6o8tcqcCgO4_crxBhy04pK3Vcb4qea_7jYw-BPAAAA___ymIEa) in a proposal the Texas Space Commission announced Friday, citing the city's 60-plus years of human spaceflight and the region's 500-plus aerospace and aviation organizations. NASA wants 300 students in class by 2028. Outgoing Gov. Greg Abbott backs the bid, and Gov.-elect Gina Hinojosa, a Democrat, [pledged to carry it forward](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGuqzAQRL8GOiN2TQwULl5Dl9feEhl7HSwZbOFNSP7-KlH-4PZnRnPm5zpfTYhhv_03G2l--jTvdJZIzHTMObBdw37jlUo2low1jraXTTO2qASAQDkby-FBM9ROL60boSYN_Xjp5AUB6lV7NSi_LAoMSSVNtyB0xg1-GDtrrcQ66HcbAErAtgVoRuyt9bIdwUIvB1V1LbnA6Wh4JaanKT6-0oOOxqatjnplzqWS_yqcKpzO82x8eqJa071w2t9QhdNbq8LpExf5SDkVKuLLiPsemJwobJiK-MiKr62wZsv3Uh_a5TPEGIrqq669bSbEzwD-428Pjb8BAAD__yf_hVU) once she takes office.

In 1968, Shirley Chisholm became the first Black woman ever elected to Congress.
That was 58 years ago.
And in all that time, Louisiana has NEVER sent a Black woman to Congress in all 214 years of statehood.
In just a few weeks, we can change that.
**This is Rep. Patricia “Pat” Moore (D-LA). On Nov. 3, I finished FIRST in Louisiana’s 5th Congressional District. On Dec. 12, I face my MAGA opponent in a runoff for the seat.**
I’ve spent 19 years fighting for families here at home, first on the Ouachita Parish Police Jury and now in the State House. I wrote a law strengthening Medicare and I’m ready to take that fight all the way to Washington.
Shirley Chisholm opened the door. **_Now it’s Louisiana’s turn to walk through it._**

Of these units, 109 apartments will go to Mainers age 55 and up, while 77 rentals will be made available for families. [...]

body:
Kristian helped break a Republican trifecta.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20261123-1&t=1&akid=4261%2E587540%2Elu2VFF)
Peter,
Three years ago, people told me I was crazy for investing in the Texas state legislature.
This month, Texans won every statewide race on the ballot and flipped the state House after more than three decades of Republican control. The candidates we backed were at the center of it.
Take **Kristian Carranza** in HD-118. In 2024, we invested over $1 million in her race, and she lost by just 3 points. Plenty of groups would have walked away. We didn’t. We backed her again in 2026.
**This year, she won by 23 points._A 26-point shift from 2024, Peter._**
And she wasn’t the only one:
* **Julio Salinas** (TX-HD-41) We helped Julio beat a “Democrat-in-name-only” opponent back in the primary to help defend this seat in the legislature.
* **Tyler Smith** (TX-HD-138) Your support fueled this incredible red-to-blue victory where Tyler beat his GOP opponent by just over 2,500 votes.
* **Christian Menefee** (TX-18) We helped Christian win a special election for this Houston seat, then spent over $400,000 to help him hold it under the GOP’s redrawn map. Now, he’ll return to serve with a Democratic majority.

This was more than a blue wave. These victories were only possible because of the long-term investment powered by grassroots supporters like you.
These new leaders are going to Austin and Washington to fix what decades of Republican rule broke: underfunded public schools, rising healthcare costs, and a government that cut breaks for corporations and billionaires while Texans paid the price.
Building sustainable movement towards progressive policies takes time. It takes trial and error, long organizing hours, hard work, and millions of dollars. You made it possible for us to back candidates and invest millions of dollars over the past 3 years to prove the doubters wrong and flip the Texas legislature.
This is why we’re investing early, recruiting candidates for 2028 _right now,_ and laying the groundwork to make the next cycle our biggest year yet. Effective movements, like the one Leaders We Deserve is building, take time. We’re starting to see our work pay off, but that just means one thing: we have to work even harder to continue the momentum.
**[The work we do now will set the stage for success in 2028. If you’re able, chip in $5 today to help us invest in candidates early, continue winning big in 2027 and 2028, and protect our wins from this year.](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20261123_tx.EvQd5G&refcode=em20261123-4261&amount=5&t=2&akid=4261%2E587540%2Elu2VFF)**

Thank you,
David Hogg

## **Part 2: The Voter Rolls, the Reckoning, and January 3, 2027**
##### **Cliff 's Note:** The piece was written by Dr. _Eric Lullove, Contributing Editor, board-certified podiatric physician, surgeon, & expert in Medicare administrative appeals._
##### _Opinions of BAM contributors do not necessarily reflect the views of BAM._
[ Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuYmx1ZWFtcC5jby9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.uXVhF6oMZVre28ZAUd7uJpjkOBLNFZfTzQWFC1Fas9g?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=226140364)
* * *
_**by Dr. Eric Lullove**_
## **Where Part 1 left off**
Part 1 followed the data. In its first hundred days, DOGE reached the payment, personnel, tax and Social Security systems of the federal government[1, 2]; after the Supreme Court lifted the Social Security injunction in June 2025, DOGE-affiliated staff copied the NUMIDENT file, the master record of every Social Security number ever issued, into a cloud environment the agency's own chief data officer could not see into[3, 4]. Executive orders in March 2025 dissolved the Privacy Act's walls between agencies[5]; CMS opened the records of 79 million Medicaid enrollees to ICE[6]; and DHS rebuilt its SAVE system, linking it to Social Security data and opening it to bulk uploads of entire state voter rolls[7, 8]. By the time the Office of Personnel Management said DOGE no longer existed, the thing DOGE existed to build was running[9]. This part is about what it was used for, how the voters answered, and who should be made to answer in the 120th Congress.
## **The voter rolls: what the data was for**
If you want to know what a database is for, watch what it is used for first. The first operational use of the consolidated federal data was not fraud recovery, not benefits integrity, not deportation logistics. It was the voter rolls, and it was timed to the midterms. It unfolded in four steps.
### _**Step one: demand every state 's voter file**_
Beginning in mid-2025, the Justice Department asked 49 states and the District of Columbia for their complete, unredacted voter registration lists: names, dates of birth, home addresses, driver's license numbers and partial Social Security numbers[10]. States were asked to sign a confidential memorandum of understanding[11]. Roughly 17 to 19 states, nearly all Republican-led, complied[12]. DOJ sued 30 states and D.C. that refused, including at least eight with Republican election chiefs[13, 12]. DOJ invoked the Help America Vote Act and the Civil Rights Act of 1960 but, in the view of election-law scholars, offered no justification for why the sensitive fields were needed[14]. Through October 2026, no district or appellate court had ruled for DOJ in any of these cases[13].
### _**Step two: run the files through SAVE**_
DOJ gave conflicting accounts of what it would do with the data until a March 2026 hearing in the Rhode Island case, where the acting chief of the Voting Section stated that the lists would be run against DHS's SAVE database[11]. Before a federal judge halted the expanded SAVE in June 2026, it had already been used to check more than 67 million registered voters, mostly from Republican-led states[15]. On September 25, 2026, the Supreme Court revived it, five weeks before Election Day[16, 17]. On October 9, a federal court ruled in the Common Cause case that DOJ's policy of collecting state lists to compare against SAVE violates voter privacy and intrudes on state authority over elections[18, 11]. Since August, USCIS has run what it calls an "Unlawful Voter Initiative" aimed at foreign-born citizens[18].
The tool is not reliable for this job. ProPublica and The Texas Tribune found DHS rushed the rebuilt SAVE into use before it could reflect voters' current citizenship, and documented citizens flagged as potential noncitizens[8]. Social Security records often do not record later naturalization[19]. Alabama's earlier attempt at the same exercise inactivated 3,251 voters and later conceded at least 2,074 were eligible[19]. A Texas county cancelled a citizen's registration because he had not yet re-proven his citizenship[20].

### _**Step three: the mail-ballot lists**_
On March 31, 2026, a second election executive order directed DHS to compile a federal list of eligible citizens and required states to send the Postal Service lists of every voter receiving a mail ballot, with the Postal Service to deliver only to those on the list[21]. A federal court in Boston declared key sections unconstitutional[22]. The Supreme Court lifted one injunction in August but in September blocked the Postal Service rules from taking effect for this election[23]. The President had said in August 2025 that with mail voting, not many Democrats would get elected[24]. That is the stated rationale, in his words.
### _**Step four: challenge the ballots**_
In the final week before the election, it all converged. DOJ, using a list it says came from federal data matching, told California it had identified about 20,000 "likely" noncitizens on the rolls and sued to force the state to segregate their ballots and not count them until citizenship was verified[25]. County officials found many on the list had no active registration and were never mailed a ballot[25]. DOJ sent similar demands for 405 voters in Washington, pressed Alaska to segregate ballots that the state said was not even possible without breaking ballot secrecy, and, under a discovery order from Chief Judge James Boasberg, disclosed it had pressed five states[26, 27, 28]. DOJ subpoenaed California election officials and reminded them they could be prosecuted; on October 31, a federal judge ordered it to stop making such threats[29].
On November 2, the day before the election, the Supreme Court rejected DOJ's California application in a one-line unsigned order with no noted dissents[30, 29]. The Ninth Circuit had already found there was no feasible way to segregate specific ballots without potentially catastrophic effects on the whole system[31]. Boasberg separately barred DOJ and DHS from demanding that California segregate ballots based on its lists[26], while finding the Democratic committees lacked standing for a nationwide injunction[32]. Asked in open court to simply promise not to send more lists, the government declined[33].

Mail voting in 2026 ran largely as it did in 2024. No state was ordered to set aside ballots. But "it mostly failed in court" is not the same as "it did not happen." The federal government assembled a cross-agency identity database, demanded every state's voter file to feed it, ran tens of millions of voters through a tool known to misflag citizens, and then, in the final week, asked courts to stop counting ballots on the strength of that output. Every step of that is on the record. The only thing in dispute is intent, and the President supplied that himself.

The machine did not work. On November 3, Democrats won control of both the House and the Senate, the first time in twenty years a Republican president has lost both chambers in a midterm[34, 35]. The President accepted the results[36].

The Anthropic IPO launched last week in record-breaking fashion valuing the company at $1.5 trillion, even as the market began to waver. Anthropic peaked at $111 on Thursday before settling down to $88 the next day. Anthropic minted thousands of new millionaires and even billionaires.
The IPO was a success, to be sure, raising $93 billion for Anthropic's dreams. But it didn't give the market reason to cheer. If anything, markets slumped, dropping 3.7% on Friday alone. The tech-heavy NASDAQ went down 5.28% in one day. The major indices entered correction territory, with tech stocks down 20% from their peak.
In related news, Nvidia stock has been faltering as thousands of employees clamor for the return of [Jensen Huang](https://substack.com/redirect/8080ecde-3772-4380-a7fa-d493e22bd181?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), whose deals have been called into question. The Board and the interim CEO said that he's not coming back, and the stock has lost $1.5 trillion or so in value.
"Okay, so what does this have to do with me?" I always hesitate to write about the stock market, because some people aren't in the market and live normal lives ignoring it. Some - like me - have most of our savings in index funds and accept some ups and downs as an ordinary course of events. On a personal level, I prefer to build and think and grow without being fixated on price fluctuations. Most of them don't matter in the long haul anyway.
All of that said, some very big things are happening right now that will affect us all. The wheels are falling off of the AI trade that has fueled both stock market prices and real economic growth - between 44 and 65% of 2026's GDP growth is attributable to the AI buildout. Compounded growth rates are slowing and the data center costs are suddenly being regarded as real money. Jensen is no longer there to guarantee billions of dollars in buildout expenses in every direction.
If the AI trade goes into reverse, it won't just be investment and retirement accounts that take a hit; we'll wind up in a recession before you know it. This will lead to the most [savage job market](https://substack.com/redirect/21eb294e-3e11-4aff-a8a9-e74971b982f8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) any of us has ever seen.
Right now the labor market is a mixed bag, a "low hire, low fire" market where job seekers are stymied by AI bot gatekeepers. Still, 2025 had 1.1 million jobs cut according to the Washington Post, an aberrantly high mark for a non-recessionary year. More money is being spent on data centers than office buildings, a clear metaphor for the slipping value of human labor.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/eedaccf4-fa8c-4baf-91c1-f2da07946a60?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The above is positively mild compared to what would happen in a recession. Most managers use bad times as a time to make [tough decisions that they've been putting off](https://substack.com/redirect/7bc53921-55ed-4e50-b929-d9a0297be496?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Imagine that fueled by AI, which will be humming along getting smarter even if valuations come crashing to earth.
I've thought for [quite some time](https://substack.com/redirect/088ed246-0a44-4cd7-932b-94095e025c79?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that people have been overly exuberant about the valuations of AI companies on the way up. Open-weight models can perform the vast majority of tasks for nickels on the dollar when compared to Anthropic's frontier models. But we all could lose on the way down if valuations crash.
Fueling the uncertainty is that AI development has led to banking websites and airlines shutting down and passwords being hacked as bad actors use new AI tools to overcome safeguards. Some of the outages are due to companies trying to improve their security before the break-in, but that's cold comfort to customers. A cybersecurity expert expects rolling service outages for 18 months as patches get installed. Get some cash out of the bank and change your passwords. Try to keep yourself in the real world, where AI doesn't have as much ability to roam.
And if the market is keeping you up at night, do what you have to do to sleep soundly. I personally think the waters get even rougher ahead.

Who won the
2020 presidential election? It’s a simple question. Todd Butler, Trump’s
crony judicial nominee, won’t answer it.

That’s the loyalty test. Trump is packing the federal courts with judges
who will deny basic reality to please him, with no regard for the
Constitution or the people.

Butler is the latest. His record shows exactly why Trump picked him:

* He gave jail officials a playbook for getting out of court-ordered
reforms. In it, civil rights groups, disability advocates, and the
Justice Department were the enemy.
* He was lead counsel for a Mississippi city and five defendants sued
over the death of Robert Loggins, a Black man who was tased and hit
with a flashlight before dying in jail.
* He backed the legal challenge that overturned a medical marijuana
measure Mississippi voters passed. The ruling took away voters’
ability to change their state constitution at the ballot box.
* A police officer let his K-9 keep tearing into a man for about half a
minute after the man was restrained. Butler defended the officer. Then
Butler’s clients tried to make the injured man pay their legal
bills.^1

Nobody assigned him these cases. For nearly 20 years in private practice,
Butler chose to stand with police and powerful institutions against the
people they hurt. If he’s confirmed, he’ll rule on our rights and freedoms
for life.

That’s Trump’s game plan: his time in power has an end date, but his
judges’ time on the bench doesn’t. Every loyalist he gets confirmed keeps
his authoritarian agenda going long after he’s gone.

Demand Justice is fighting to stop Trump’s cronies. We expose their
records, build the pressure to keep them off our courts, and make sure
voters know which senators wave them through.

In solidarity,

TO: Congress
FROM: Willis
Subject: Abolish the Electoral College now!

To the members of Congress,

**I am writing today to DEMAND that you abolish the Electoral College!**

Time and time again, Republicans have won the presidency despite LOSING the popular vote.

_Donald Trump wouldn’t have even won in the first place if it wasn’t for the Electoral College._

Every American’s vote should be counted equally. This system is TOTALLY UNDEMOCRATIC and UNFAIR!

**So I’m demanding you do what’s right for our democracy and ensure our presidents are chosen by the PEOPLE.**

[I’m signing this letter today to DEMAND you abolish the Electoral College as soon as possible. Trump is backing Republican National Committee Chair Joe Gruters, who's being challenged by the committee's second-in-command, KC Crosbie. After a midterm loss like that, of course people are going to ask what the hell happened and who should be in charge going into 2028.
We did this after Kamala Harris lost. Democrats were asking how we could lose to Trump again. Then we got an autopsy I thought was complete bullshit. I'm curious whether Republicans will get any closer to an honest answer about their own losses.

name: Gina Hinojosa
subject: An important update about our campaign.
body:
You won’t see a single fundraising request from me or my campaign from mid-December through late June. Here’s what that means right now:
# [](https://governorhinojosa.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Thank you, Peter.
Together, we won a historic victory that shocked Texas and the nation. As you read this, my team and I are in the process of building out our transition team so we can deliver for Texans starting Day One.
But there’s something you should know. In just 19 days, we’ll be legally prohibited from fundraising for the next six months.
Let me explain why this matters: The Texas Ethics Commission bars statewide officeholders, legislators, and political action committees from raising money during the regular legislative session. Which means, from December 13th through June 20th, we’ll have to shut down our fundraising completely.
Peter, you won’t see a single fundraising request from me or my campaign from mid-December through late June.
During that time, we won’t need a lot of money, but we’ll still have bills to pay. And the billionaires who tried to buy this election aren’t going anywhere. They’re already plotting to stop our agenda, so we have to stay funded and organized for the fights that await just around the corner.
We only have a little over two weeks to raise what we need. Which is why I’m asking: **[Peter, will you make a contribution of any amount today to make sure we have the resources we need before the fundraising freeze begins?](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20261123_1_freeze.7PR5zl&refcode=em20261123-2692&amount=5&t=1&akid=2692%2E299639%2EvKjI9s)**

Thank you again for your support.

# **DNC announces 12 presidential primary debates for 2028 cycle**
Democrats will hold **[12 primary debates](https://substack.com/redirect/ad90242a-b119-4652-ad1a-bfa10744fb2c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** starting in June, with five in 2027 and seven in 2028, capping each at 20 qualifying candidates across two nights if needed, mirroring the large-field format used in 2020.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/ad90242a-b119-4652-ad1a-bfa10744fb2c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **The announcement follows Democrats ' sweeping midterm wins,** with Chairman Ken Martin emphasizing party unity heading into 2028; qualification criteria will include polling benchmarks and grassroots fundraising, similar to past cycles.
* **For the first time, candidates must pledge to disavow dark money to participate.** More scheduling details, including locations, come in January, as the DNC also finalizes its 2028 convention city among Boston, Denver, and Philadelphia.

* * *
# **Ukraine strikes Russian ships off Libya as war expands beyond Black Sea**
Ukraine claimed responsibility for **[sinking the Russian corvette Merkury](https://substack.com/redirect/ee87ed73-6272-4062-8eb4-37a1d9389345?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and a helicopter near Benghazi, Libya, plus damaging a cargo vessel used to transport weapons, with Zelenskyy touting the operation as a direct response to Russian aggression using Ukrainian-made naval drones.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/ee87ed73-6272-4062-8eb4-37a1d9389345?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **The strike adds to a pattern of Ukrainian attacks reaching far beyond traditional battle zones,** including a recent fire aboard a Russian cargo ship in the Gulf of Finland and suspected Ukrainian drone involvement in a Mediterranean tanker incident earlier this year.
* **The expanding campaign comes as U.S.-backed peace talks resumed** after a nine-month pause, with analysts suggesting Ukraine is pursuing "horizontal escalation" to gain leverage since neither side can force battlefield concessions, even as disputes over Russian-occupied territory remain unresolved.

* * *
# **Western intelligence warns Russia may launch nuclear space weapon next month**
Intelligence shared among NATO allies suggests Russia's dormant satellite, Sputnik-S, capable of carrying a nuclear warhead, **[could launch as soon as next month,](https://substack.com/redirect/ac6e72c4-124f-4086-82e6-35bdb58496d6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** according to Bloomberg, a move that would violate the 1967 Outer Space Treaty Russia signed.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/ac6e72c4-124f-4086-82e6-35bdb58496d6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **The U.S. Defense Intelligence Agency reported in October that Russia is developing a satellite weapon** potentially capable of disabling thousands of satellites, while Germany's government said it's taking the reports seriously; Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov dismissed the claims Monday.
* **Putin previously denied plans to deploy nuclear weapons in space,** insisting Russia's space activities mirror those of other nations. A space researcher called the reports "nuclear saber-rattling," noting such an attack would also damage Russia's own satellite infrastructure.

* * *
# **Divider-in-Chief: Obama says Democrats represent America, Republicans represent white America**
Former President Barack Obama praised newly elected House Democrats, contrasting what **[he described falsely as the white racial homogeneity](https://substack.com/redirect/90b44580-d3e0-4a30-82b9-94618ffdc74c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** of Republican lawmakers with the supposed diversity of Democrats, calling their caucus representative of "America" itself.

name: Wes Moore
subject: None of this was inevitable
body:
# [](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/8?t=1&akid=2328%2E1086043%2EGaX_1N)
**_“How do you possibly think you can win?”_**
Peter, it’s Wes. When I first ran for governor, people asked me that all the time.
It wasn’t just because we were polling at 1%. It was because nobody thought someone who looked like me could lead Maryland. It was never about whether we were qualified. It was about whether we were “electable.”
My answer to the question was always: **Because I know our full history.**
And it’s not only the doors closed to us. It’s the people who fought for us without knowing us, who believed in the hope of us, and who knew they would never live to see that hope realized.
This November, that hope was realized in four states at once. Voters didn’t ask who looked “electable.” They asked who would fight for them and their families, and they elected a total of five Black governors, as well as the first Black woman to lead a U.S. Territory — the most in history.
[](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20261123-1.wQzLu4&refcode=em-20261123-1&t=2&akid=2328%2E1086043%2EGaX_1N)
_Wes and newly elected Black Democratic governors-elect_
Democrats won all over because they promised to fight for working families everywhere. None of this was inevitable. Every one of those firsts happened because people fought for it – and none of it is guaranteed.
That’s why we must fight for it every year, in every election.
Elevate,
Wes Moore

name: Jeff Walter
subject: They ran on affordability. Where’s the plan?
body:
Before the new Congress is sworn in, Democrats owe families an answer.

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/jeffwalterforcongress/they-ran-on-affordability-wheres-the-plan?e=fa724b03ca)
---
|
---
| | | | | |

Friend,Democrats spent the campaign promising to make life more affordable. The new Congress hasn’t even been sworn in, and Democrats are only talking about investigations and impeachments. Here’s what I’d like to hear from them: What’s your plan to bring down the cost of groceries, lower energy bills, and make it easier for working families to get ahead?Families can’t put off paying the electric bill until Washington gets around to affordability. Congress should come in on day one ready to work on the issues people sent them there to solve not partisan lawfare. That’s why I’m asking you to [**chip in $25, $50, or whatever you can today**](https://us.list-manage.com/dxpt5eJ8bA6?e=fa724b03ca&c2id=02d8faed9a08421996be4d5fd2cd9a20). Your contribution will help me get my message out and hold Democrats accountable for the affordability promises they made on the campaign trail.[**Donate today**](https://us.list-manage.com/8_BcF9bR34H?e=fa724b03ca&c2id=02d8faed9a08421996be4d5fd2cd9a20) They asked voters to judge them on affordability. Let’s take them at their word.Thank you,
Jeff Walter

Let’s be abundantly clear:
Black women are the backbone of the Democratic Party.
Last week, 93% of Black women voted for Democrats. They knocked the doors. They organized their churches, their families, and their neighborhoods. They turned out across the Deep South in numbers that stunned the experts, and they delivered the blue wave that just won us the House and the Senate.
Every time our backs were against the wall, Black women showed up.
And far too often, the party thanked them with a speech and then moved on.
Not this time.
**On December 12, we have a chance to do more than say thank you. We have a chance to make history.** **Rep. Patricia “Pat” Moore (D) is headed to a runoff. If she wins, she’ll be the first Black woman Louisiana has EVER sent to Congress. ** Pat has spent 19 years serving her community in Monroe, first on the Ouachita Parish Police Jury and now in the state House. She’s exactly the kind of leader Black women have built this party around for generations, and exactly the kind of leader they deserve to see in Washington.
But MAGA won’t hand this seat over. Republicans have held it since 2004, and they’ll fight with everything they have to keep it.
Black women have shown up for Democrats every single time. Now it’s our turn to show up for them.

name: Katherine Clark
subject: Let’s get to work!

body:
Throughout my life and in Congress, I’ve worked to build consensus, find creative solutions, and fight – for women, for families, and for working people.
| Friend, we just made history.

**It’s Katherine Clark, and I’m honored to be part of the team that will lead our Caucus as the House Majority Leader in the 120th Congress, and incredibly proud to be the very first woman to hold this position.**

I don’t take this lightly. For every woman who was told she couldn't lead, every family fighting to get ahead, and every American who deserves a government that works for them: I am ready for this fight.

I am so grateful to have been chosen by my colleagues not only to make history, but also to lead our record-breaking, history-making majority forward as we fight for freedom and economic opportunity, for democracy and for upholding our values, and for every American to have the opportunity to get ahead. [But making history is only the beginning — now it’s time to deliver the results. That’s why we need to build up our resources starting TODAY. My team is setting a goal to raise $5,000 to kickstart our work in this new Congress. Friend, will you split a donation between the Voter Protection Project and me today?](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/146886?t=6&akid=31812%2E878179%2EwdhF_Y) | [Donate »](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/146886?t=7&akid=31812%2E878179%2EwdhF_Y)
---
On Election Day, voters affirmed Democrats’ commitment to working people and families. They sent a message loud and clear — that our work is far from done — and that the American people need to remain in focus no matter which party holds the speaker’s gavel.

For the past two years, House Republicans have used the far-right trifecta in Washington to sow division in America, but House Democrats’ strength comes from our unity of purpose.

**Our mission remains the same: build an America that works for everyone.**

That means lowering costs at the grocery store and the gas pump, ending the reckless war in Iran, reversing Republicans’ catastrophic cuts to healthcare, and pursuing _rigorous_ oversight of this corrupt administration.
[As Majority Leader, I’m willing and ready to partner with anyone fighting on the side of the American people. And friend, if you’re ready to roll up your sleeves and get to work with us, please split a contribution of any amount between the Voter Protection Project and me to help us reach our goal and begin to pave the path to progress »](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/146886?t=8&akid=31812%2E878179%2EwdhF_Y)
If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your split donation between Katherine Clark and VPP will go through immediately:
[CONTRIBUTE $10 »](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/146887?t=9&akid=31812%2E878179%2EwdhF_Y)
---

[CONTRIBUTE $100 »](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/146890?t=12&akid=31812%2E878179%2EwdhF_Y)
[Or a custom donation »](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/146891?t=13&akid=31812%2E878179%2EwdhF_Y)
I came to Washington to fight for women, working families, and communities that are too often left out. At every step of this journey, you have been in my corner. I am so glad to have you by my side as we break the glass ceiling today, and I hope to have your trust and support in all that’s to come.

Thank you. Truly.

Katherine Clark
House Majority Leader-elect
