Patriot,

For more than five years, a group of January 6 Patriots, many of them veterans who served this country honorably, carried a weight most Americans can't imagine: **politically charged trials, years behind bars, and a government that treated them like enemies of the state. **

President Trump commuted their sentences and set them free. But he never pardoned them, so their convictions stayed on the books and followed them everywhere.

Here's what happened next.

**First:** the Department of Justice asked a federal appeals court to vacate those convictions once and for all.

**Then:** Rep. Jamie Raskin, one of the most partisan Democrats in Washington, D.C., filed a petition to block it. He opposed the DOJ in all three appeals and demanded the court appoint a special lawyer to defend the original jury verdicts. _His goal was to keep these Patriots branded as criminals for the rest of their lives_.

**That 's when Stand in the Gap Foundation stepped in.** We funded the defense team so they could answer Raskin on time and with strength. The attorneys worked through the weekend to meet a very tight deadline, and they filed.

**Now:** the convictions have been vacated and the cases dismissed. Raskin's effort to keep the old verdicts alive did not stop it.

They tried to stop it. They failed.

That's a victory worth celebrating. But it isn't the end of the story...

[They need your help to rebuild their lives, which is exactly what Stand in the Gap Foundation exists to do. You can show your support by donating today.](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABl7ImQiOjUwNzAsInQiOjc2NywicyI6MTJ9AAwAAAAABEpiQ9ED25vdCNScgll6mzFCocjwjeTtFTrTWHA4xKFKGq5OomM0zNnH2JT8sdNa7Muekt_ERQKzsi7OhmCvZZAo8ymGZZLK4cq-nMPw)

Legal forgiveness is only the beginning.

A court order can wipe a conviction off the record, but it can't pay back years of legal bills, restore lost careers, or rebuild a reputation the media spent half a decade destroying.

These men and women walked out of prison financially drained, publicly smeared as _" insurrectionists"_ and _" terrorists,"_ and starting over from nothing.

**Stand in the Gap Foundation exists for this moment. Your gift today helps us:**
>>> Cover remaining legal costs so no Patriot is left defenseless against the next attack;

>>> Relieve the crushing debt left behind by years of litigation; and

>>> Provide reentry support so these Americans can find stable housing, return to work, and rebuild their lives.
The radical Left lost in court.

**_But if these Patriots are left broke and broken, the Left still gets what it wanted_.**

We can't let that happen, Patriot.

# [](https://act.fordfornevada.com/go/12?t=1&akid=1283%2E127862%2Es8f35c)
Folks,
I am humbled to be emailing you as Governor-elect of our great state of Nevada.
_You_ made this happen. Every vote cast, phone call made, door knocked, and dollar donated by this grassroots team played a role in our historic victory.
But what happened on Election Night was not the end. It was only the beginning. **And****, it is time to get to work!**
As a key member of the team that powered this victory, you deserve to know exactly what I’m focusing on over these next couple weeks:
→ Staffing up our official team so we’re ready to get to work on Day One
→ Setting up committees that will help us build coalitions and govern effectively
→ Preparing for a new chapter for Nevada
**All of these priorities require resources that can fund this urgent work – and unfortunately, we spent our bank account down to zero fighting to secure this seat.** That is why I must ask our strongest supporters like you if you’d be willing to keep fueling our team through Inauguration Day.
**[Will you pitch in $5 to fuel our transition so we can hit the ground running in the new year?](https://act.fordfornevada.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_af_20261123_1_ak.JIonox&amount=5&refcode=em20261123-1283&t=3&akid=1283%2E127862%2Es8f35c)**

Democrat Courtney Scheff defeated longtime District 5 Councilman Mike Gallagher in November, leaving Democrats set to hold all 11 seats on Cuyahoga County Council. I spoke with Gallagher, the council's last Republican, about what he saw on Election Day, how the next council might exercise its independence, and which spending decisions he'll be watching.
_This conversation has been condensed and paraphrased for clarity._
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f9c19932-e795-43f8-b3d6-547d39fbc555?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
County Councilman District 5 Mike Gallagher
* * *
**Matt Diemer:** You've held this seat a long time. Were you expecting to lose? When did you realize something was happening?
**Mike Gallagher:** I didn't see it coming until Election Day. By 10 that morning I could feel something in the air. People going in to vote seemed focused, like they had a mission. The message I took from it was that they wanted to get rid of what was going on in Columbus and Washington. That was my read of the people I was seeing that morning.
* * *
**Matt Diemer:** How much do you think Trump affected your race?
**Mike Gallagher:** Some. Maybe a point or two. I've always tried to reach people in the middle and on the other side. A president can affect races down the ballot. Biden affected previous elections, and you'd expect Trump to have an effect here. What got me was that he told people to vote like he was on the ballot. Then afterward he said Republicans would have won if he had been on it. As far as I'm concerned, he was on the ballot in this district. People were thinking about him when they voted.
* * *
**Matt Diemer:** What mattered more to you, the top of the ticket or what the parties did on the ground? I barely saw the Republican Party anywhere.
**Mike Gallagher:** Neither did I. I thought the top of our ticket was weak. People hoped it would get stronger as the race went on. Then Vivek Ramaswamy ran that ad involving Amy Acton's biological mother. I've never gone negative in a campaign, and I'm proud of that. I thought that ad was unnecessary. Running it that late told me he thought he was losing.
The Democrats saw an opening and went for it. I'd see two or three of them at polling places while I was walking around looking for anybody on our side. I give them credit for showing up. It felt like a ghost town for Republicans. The last time I remember speaking with county party chair Lisa Stickan was over the summer. I had support from individual Republicans. As the statewide and congressional races got messier, I told the party to leave me off its materials and let me run my own race. I wonder how it would have gone if I'd run as an independent.
* * *
**Matt Diemer:** Democrats will have every seat on council and the county executive's office. Will voters still hear disagreements in public? Can council hold Chris Ronayne accountable?
**Mike Gallagher:** I think it can. People called me the lone voice. I was the loudest voice, and I had colleagues who shared my concerns, depending on the issue. If I saw something wrong, I said something. I also thought the way Patrick Kelly was treated sent a message about the price of breaking ranks. That's how I saw it.
Watch who chairs finance and who gets the other committee chairs. Within six months, we should have a sense of whether council will serve as the check on the executive that it was intended to be. They can work with him and still exercise their own judgment.
* * *
**Matt Diemer:** You've been one of the loudest critics of Ronayne's spending. Where do you think he's put the county at risk? What's the first decision you'll be watching?
**Mike Gallagher:** Start with the quarter-percent sales tax extension for 40 years. The case for it was that we needed to build a jail and a justice center. My concern is how much of that money can go toward covering general fund spending. I tried to make that case during the campaign, and it didn't resonate.
I'll watch where the new Health and Human Services levy money goes. The county went back to voters two years early. My criticism is that the administration spent down reserves and went to the public without a plan to replenish them. If the county uses the new revenue to replace everything Washington and Columbus stopped funding after COVID, I think we're going to be in trouble. I've also heard talk of going to voters for money for the pro sports facilities. I think that would be a much harder sell.
We also have hundreds of county positions sitting open. It used to be that people really wanted to work for the county. I'm curious what happens to some of those positions as AI comes into use, and whether that saves the county money.
* * *
**Matt Diemer:** Is this a make-or-break two years for the county budget? How much room does council have to get things wrong?
**Mike Gallagher:** I don't know if I'd call it make-or-break. The big decisions are coming quickly. I remember the jail being discussed at roughly $550 million. I think it could end up costing $1.2 billion or more. Then there's the justice center. The judiciary is frustrated, and we'll have to borrow for another major project. When we handed it over, we were talking about $600 million, with Cleveland paying about a third if it participated. As far as I know, we're still waiting to hear where Cleveland stands. How do you design a building when you don't know if one of the partners is going to be in it?
* * *
**Matt Diemer:** How do you think Dale Miller has handled the council presidency? Who would you look at for the job?
**Mike Gallagher:** I was in leadership in Strongsville. It's a hard job. You're dealing with personalities and whatever problems come through the door that day. I thought Ellen Connally was the right person at the right time. Dan Brady was politically savvy, and we dealt with problems as they came up. With Dale, I kept hearing that he'd run things by the executive team first. I thought that was more deference than the job called for. It made for a difficult two years.
Michael Houser, Robert Schleper and Meredith Turner come to mind. I don't know if Schleper wants it. For the new members coming in, I'd spend some time absorbing how things work. People hear "council" and think of city council. A lot of county council's work is legislative and administrative. You're figuring out where money needs to go and making sure problems get to the right people.
* * *
**Matt Diemer:** What advice would you give Courtney Scheff as she takes over your seat?
**Mike Gallagher:** I've met with her. I'd tell her to be independent, keep her eyes and ears open and pay attention to how things unfold. I don't remember Ed FitzGerald or Armond Budish calling council members about votes. Chris is comfortable doing that. For me, once I've heard the debate and participated in it, I know how I'm going to vote. That's my responsibility as a council member.
* * *
**Matt Diemer:** Do you think Cleveland is pulling its weight in its relationship with the county?
**Mike Gallagher:** Cleveland relies heavily on the county, in my view. The councils don't meet, and I don't know how much the mayor and county executive coordinate. Before we get to the money, I'd like us to sit down and ask where we're going. The city has a direction and the county has a direction. I don't see those lining up very well right now.
When Ed FitzGerald announced a $50 million program to tear down problem houses and clear properties, three Cleveland council members showed up at the next meeting. One told me Cleveland should get the whole amount because it had the biggest problems. I asked how much of his own ward allocation he'd already spent on tearing down houses. I ended up putting in a records request about the ward money and withdrew it after a colleague asked me to. I still remember that exchange.
* * *
**Matt Diemer:** What's next for you? Are we making news today about a run for state Senate?
**Mike Gallagher:** I'm going to give it a little while and relax. I've been retired, but I've always worked. I'm not pursuing anything right now. The county Republican Party has some work to do to figure out what it wants to be. We did horribly in this election.
I really do want the people who got elected to succeed. I need Amy Acton to succeed. I need Courtney to succeed. I need Chris to succeed. If they do well, we all do well. We haven't reached our potential. I'm interested in what's happening at the lakefront, and I'm glad the Haslams and Dan Gilbert are investing here. I'd like to see more young people come back home.
* * *

**November 23, 2026**
With some work underway in our home, I have been moving things around to make room for it. Somewhere along the way, my Chanukah decorations and games have disappeared in the process. Things from this room are in that room, and things from that room are, hmm, where are they?
I put everything into two boxes and tucked them somewhere safe.
The menorah, last year's themed napkins and plates, a fantastic recipe for jelly-filled doughnuts, and the dreidels. My granddaughter will appreciate those this year! Ah, and the candles.
There is a strange irony in how we treat meaningful things: we bury them for safekeeping.
But traditions are not decorations. They are the continuity of a story that began long before we arrived. Faith is not what we say; it is what we preserve.
_Ay yi yi! The boxes! Everything preserved, and nothing to be found?_
**Pause.
Breathe.
Look Deeper.**
**Refuel.**
**Welcome to Sweet Ground.**

body:

| | | I've been thinking a lot about road trips this week. When I was a kid, my family didn't take many vacations. When we did travel, we brought our own food, and my parents planned every stop. They made sure we had what we needed before we set out, because once you're on the highway, you can't turn back for what you forgot. **_That's how I've come to think about this fight._** For the last two years, the road has been long, and a lot of it has been downright hard. We watched the safety net that saved my family get gutted. We watched hate become a strategy. We watched a president turn the government against his critics and treat the White House like a family business. There were stretches where it was hard to see where we were going at all. Then came November... Kansas sent a Democrat to the Senate for the first time since 1932. Texas, Alaska, Arizona, and Florida delivered wins that almost nobody predicted. After a long stretch of hard road, it felt like pulling into an oasis. **This Thanksgiving, I'm grateful for that oasis, and I'm grateful for you. ** Every volunteer who knocked a door, every donor who chipped in, and everyone who read these emails and refused to give up made it possible.Election Day felt like a great oasis amidst the arduous journey of the Trump 2.0 era. That’s a phenomenal accomplishment, and I don’t want to understate it. However, we’d be lying to ourselves if we said the trip was finished.We can't stay at this oasis. We need to finish what we started. **This road trip ends in 2029, when we evict MAGA extremism out of the White House, elect a Democratic supermajority in Congress, and finally get to work passing laws that give working families a real shot. That means fair wages, lower costs, good schools in every zip code, and an economy where hard work still leads somewhere.** That's a long drive, and the most important part of a long drive happens before you leave: you restock, refuel, and make sure you have what you need for the road ahead. That's what this end-of-year push is about for Equal Opportunity Now. Every dollar we raise now is fuel in the tank for the races that will decide whether we finish this trip. **[Before you head into the holiday, help us fill the tank. Chip in $15 or $40 to Equal Opportunity Now, and let's hit the road running.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/143938919/661881425/1090555623?refcode=261123_ngp_roadtrip&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDUvMS83MzE2OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJlNzk1Y2UxMS03OWU3LWYxMTEtOTFmMy0wMDBkM2E1MzM5NzgiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=QzO6s0zrlma_J_dm1JlkQYLQNHHAvt-JBjfgsGNa41I=)**

Demand governors act. | | | Friend, Governors have a critical role to play in preventing their constituents from losing Medicaid and SNAP benefits in the new year. Right now, governors have until December 11 to opt in to a six-month delay in Republicans’ mandated Medicaid work-reporting requirements that are expected to kick 10 million people off of Medicaid next year. Governors must also pressure Congress to undo SNAP cuts and SNAP cost-shifts to states that threaten state budgets and millions of people’s access to nutrition assistance. I will keep fighting in Congress to undo the harm done by Republicans’ Big Betrayal Bill right now in year-end spending bills and next year in the new Congress. My colleagues need to hear from their governors to act with the urgency our communities need. Thank you for taking action today, Rashida \---------- Forwarded message --------- From: Rashida Tlaib** Date: Sat, Nov 21, 2026 Subject: [take action] Demand governors take immediate action to prevent Medicaid and SNAP cuts To: dpwillis67@gmail.com Friend, Our fight to reverse the harm done by congressional Republicans doesn’t need to wait until new Democratic majorities are sworn in in January. Our communities need support now. When Republicans passed their Big Betrayal Bill in 2025, they slashed critical programs like Medicaid and SNAP to hand tax breaks to billionaires and corporations. It’s estimated that if Medicaid work-reporting requirements go into effect, 10 million people could lose their health care coverage**. And since passage of the bill, 5.5 million people have already lost nutrition assistance , including millions of kids. But right now, our governors can take action to protect people who rely on Medicaid and SNAP. For the next three weeks, the administration is allowing governors to sign onto a 6-month delay in Medicaid work-reporting requirements. And hopefully in that window, our new Democratic-controlled Congress can do away with them entirely. Most people on Medicaid already work, but often in jobs with inconsistent hours, making it hard to meet Republicans’ new reporting requirements. And, if people simply don’t have time to wade through the red tape each month, they could be dropped from Medicaid even though they qualify. Additionally, when Congress passed its Big Betrayal Bill, it not only cut SNAP benefits, it also shifted more of the cost responsibility to states. That means that as governors and state legislators begin crafting their 2027 budgets in the new year, they’ll have to decide between covering SNAP benefits for their residents or paying for other vital programs. Some may choose to opt out ofSNAP entirely. With only about three weeks left for Congress to act after the Thanksgiving holiday, I’m demanding year-end government spending bills that undo the harm that Republicans did to SNAP , and at minimum, delay the cost-shift to states. Since this cost shift directly impacts states’ budgets, congressional delegations need to hear from governors immediately. ** Our communities are hurting. We can’t wait months for action. Thankfully, there are actions that governors can take right now. They just need to hear from us. Thank you for demanding urgent action to protect our neighbors, families, and communities. Do you support permitting reform? | [ ](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/143939539/661883122/987221411?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNi8xLzk4MjcyIiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjhhNzY5OWJlLTdiZTctZjExMS05MWYzLTAwMGQzYTUzMzk3OCIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=zD9qfHgtzDVGwy5XGquSvwQ6YPZJDdO7vUl1leRG6Y0=&emci=66e047b8-7be7-f111-91f3-000d3a533978&emdi=8a7699be-7be7-f111-91f3-000d3a533978&ceid=15125741)
---

On November 19th, the Minnesota State Canvassing Board met at the Minnesota Judicial Center as required by the [Minnesota Constitution](https://substack.com/redirect/c57cde7f-f755-4a1e-b6b9-4c6db25f460c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Under this Constitutional provision, the Board is to "declare the result" of "every election for officeholders elected statewide." If you want to see the actual report, click [here](https://substack.com/redirect/fe1a7408-7137-40c0-82bf-59ba788931e9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), but do not expect to see the report as you will need to request a copy by email. 1
The official canvass 2 is part of Minnesota's post-election review process. [Minn. Stat. 204C.33](https://substack.com/redirect/ae2d84a2-d578-484d-8e39-89c62dc85d5e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) divides responsibility between county canvassing boards and the State Canvassing Board. County boards canvass the returns in their own counties and declare the winners of county races and state offices voted on entirely within one county. The State Canvassing Board canvasses the certified county reports and declares the winners of federal offices and state offices voted on in more than one county.

In way of a real world example, DFL Candidate Amanda Matchett in Minnesota House District 23A had an election held exclusively within the borders of Anoka County. Following her _request for a recount_ , Anoka County will be administering the recount on November 23rd at 9:00 am, and its County Canvas Board is scheduled to certify the final results on November 24th. In contrast, the Minnesota State Senate contest in [SD#4 covers](https://substack.com/redirect/a6eb970f-b912-4ef3-a6c5-341d78c3cf2d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Becker and Clay Counties, so the recount is controlled by the State Canvassing Board. This past Thursday, The State Canvassing Board confirmed that DFL Challenger Robert Kupec _requested a recount_ , which has[ been set for](https://substack.com/redirect/5c7a5ea4-101c-4b7f-86c3-e0a45d9401c6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) November 23rd and 24th.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/29f86775-7558-457e-a27f-de5e27cc4cf5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
### State Canvassing Board sets Schedule and Establishes the Rules of the Recount.
At its November 19 meeting, the State Canvassing Board approved the recount plan for Minnesota's First Congressional District (CD1) The [recount dates and times ](https://substack.com/redirect/5c7a5ea4-101c-4b7f-86c3-e0a45d9401c6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)and the Rules of the recount were established. I'll explain my concerns about the recount procedures below. The State Canvassing Board ["recessed"](https://substack.com/redirect/46a40dbc-7ba9-4e52-aa3e-89beb297e960?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) its meeting and will reconvene on December 8 at 2 p.m. to review and certify the results of the recounts.
The Congressional District recount spans 21-counties and is scheduled to occur in each individual county starting the Monday after Thanksgiving weekend (November 30th) through December 3rd. In general, "A recount is a process to precisely determine the vote count between two candidates whose vote margin is extremely close. During a recount, election officials individually review each ballot that was cast on Election Day." The Secretary of State provides an [overview](https://substack.com/redirect/14fa73da-1b39-4c68-aa54-e64e8faee2dc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of this process. The official recount handbook can be found here ___>
| Recount Guide 20181.2MB ∙ PDF file
---|---
| [Download](https://substack.com/redirect/521f441e-f638-4632-b9a3-85d3d50a2c3c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
---
From a high level, each individual ballot is examined by election officials and sorted into piles for each candidate under review. The governing determination is [voter intent](https://substack.com/redirect/fe49e8d2-cf19-41e9-8155-06ee2beac4b1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and each campaign has volunteers present watching the process who can challenge the election officials determination of which candidate pile the ballot goes into. This is done on a ballot by ballot basis and requires close scrutiny by the election officials and the campaign representatives.
The week after Thanksgiving the recount process will be in full swing throughout Southern Minnesota. This process is _civics in action_ and a chance for you to participate and see firsthand how this process works. if you's like to take part, the Finstad campaign is requesting that those interested submit a request to volunteer [HERE](https://substack.com/redirect/6b97bee6-3341-48c5-b757-90ed2c39d1de?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
I will be in Olmsted County starting on Tuesday December 1st where they are scheduled to have at least 20 active tables. Participating in the recount process is a fantastic way for you to watch the post-election process in action These processes need to undergo bright sunshine and scrutiny. The more the election process is hidden behind a curtain, the less liberty can flourish.
# The Great Ballot Mixing - Breaking the Chain of Custody.
Many concerns have been raised regarding the election process which all deserve scrutiny. One process I have followed very closely this year was the implementation of the early in-person voting process. As explained in an [earlier substack](https://substack.com/redirect/a1fcbee5-549b-4b0d-8cca-517dfc75a1d1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) post, "Early Voting locations will no longer be placed into individual absentee-ballot envelopes for later review by an absentee ballot board. Instead, after completing the required procedures, the voter will place the ballot **directly into the ballot counter. "**
At the time of writing my original substack post, I found it somewhat reassuring that there was a daily reconcilation process that kept the early in-person ballots separate so that the process could be scrutized if and when it became necessary. 3
Well that time has now come - in the form a post election recount and preparing for a possible election challenge. I have requested early in-person voting records from various County election officials to confirm that these requirement were properly followed. While many juriscitions have kept these ballots separate, under guidance from the Secretary of State, the absentee ballots have been mixed and comingled with the early in-person ballots - the photo below clearly shows folded ballots (absentee) being mixed with unfolded ballots (early in-person):
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/6aaed852-46d4-4f62-b81a-94cdc6fd39d1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The early in-person statute [(203B.30)](https://substack.com/redirect/b8e754c6-57df-45d6-a83e-2927f1474a88?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) requires that the voter be "current" in the SVRS and affirmatively "confirm" that they have not already cast a ballot. Shockingly, throughout the State, there were invididuals who were allowed to vote and place their ballot directly into the ballot counter without being entered into the SVRS system. If this error can be properly establihed in a court challenge, these ballots should be excluded from the totoal vote count. The public should expect that the separation of ballots, as required by state law, should continue throughout the post-election review and recount process.
Despite repeated requests from the campaign to see the proposed recount plan in advance, the Secretary of State only disclosed the plan by dropping it on the table outside the canvass meeting either moments prior our during the actual meeting time. A copy of this plan is here -->
| Cd1 Recount Plan 20261.71MB ∙ PDF file
---|---
| [Download](https://substack.com/redirect/2ee0822c-7672-41fd-98e7-4b93d2a1a85a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
---
Note the language in paragraph 3 of the recount procedures:
3. All ballots cast on Election Day, absentee ballots (including absentee/mail ballots and early voting ballots will be counted. _**The polling place ballots will be combined with the absentee/mail ballots and early voting ballots to be counted for each precinct, and all ballots for the precinct will be counted and reported together as one total.**_

In other words, the Secretary of State (without advance disclosure of the proposed plan to the public or the recount campaign) empowered the State Canvassing Board to attempt to override Minnesota law to mix these ballots and destroy the clearly established chain of custody requirements.
Once these ballots are mixed, the chain of custody keeping the early in-person ballots separate has been broken. This matters as during an election contest, the validity of these very ballots can be challenged.
Efforts are under way to try and prevent the destrution of the chain of custody separation of these ballots. More to follow as the post-election scrutiny continues.

What I also discovered was that the agenda and the materials to be released at the Thursday State Canvass Board meeting were not posted in advance of the meeting. When I arrived at the Minnesota Supreme Court Chambers prior to the meeting, the only document on the table outside was the official "agenda." At some time after I arrived additional documents were placed on this table which included the all important "recount plan" which will be discussed in detail in this article.

---
Hi Friend, Did you know that the Christmas story begins hundreds of years before Jesus was born? Long before Mary and Joseph traveled to Bethlehem, the prophet Isaiah spoke of a Child who would come. A Son who would be given. A Savior who would bring light into a world living in darkness. And then, centuries later, God fulfilled His promise. A baby was born in Bethlehem, just as the Scriptures foretold. His name was Jesus, and He came to do what none of us could do for ourselves: save us from our sins and reconcile us to God. | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | Hi there,
On Election Day, more than 1.5 million Coloradans voted to invest Colorado's dollars in Colorado. We won by more than 20 points.
Over the course of the campaign we drove 30,000 miles—more than the circumference of the planet—and heard from folks across the state who are struggling to afford housing, utility bills, child care, groceries, and more. We heard about what it costs to build a life here, and how that cost just keeps going up.
We went from Alamosa to Adams County, Fort Collins to Fort Morgan, Steamboat to Sterling. And Pueblo. Lots of trips to Pueblo.

Instead of parking the state's dollars in Wall Street and Washington, I'll put them to work building Colorado. Housing, renewable energy, infrastructure. Colorado dollars for Colorado.
In the Bridges household, we believe a campaign done right is good for the soul. Ours and our democracy's. Thank you to those who have been here since the beginning, and to those just joining the adventure.
I'm grateful to the folks who took the time to talk with us, whether I knocked on their door or they came out to an event, and especially grateful to have my family onstage with me on Election Night. The way we won reflects what we believe.
I'm energized by the challenge to align our state's investments with our values. The transition is underway, and I take office in January. More on the great team we're building coming soon.
We can't wait to get to work!
And I really look forward to the next 30,000 miles.

name: Chad Bianco
subject: Don't Believe the Headlines
body:
Sacramento's crime numbers don't match what my deputies see every day.

| | | | | |
---
| |

My fellow Californians,
Last week Sacramento put out a press release bragging about "record low crime" in California. I'd love for that to be true. But that's not what my deputies are seeing.
They're seeing the same repeat offenders arrested again and again. **Retail theft crews are hitting store after store. One ring was just tied to 24 burglaries across the state. And fentanyl is still taking our kids.** Crime numbers look a lot better when people stop reporting crimes because nothing happens to the criminals.
**Here in Riverside County, we don't spin numbers. We make arrests.** Just last week, my deputies ran a single operation in Perris and arrested eight shoplifters.
That's how you keep a community safe. You enforce the law, and you stand behind the men and women who do it. If you believe California needs sheriffs who still enforce the law, I'd be grateful to have you with me. **I am running for re-election as Sheriff of Riverside County, and I would be grateful for your support.**
God bless you, and God bless Riverside County.
**Sheriff Chad Bianco
Riverside County**

subject: The Worst Used Car You Can Buy Right Now

If the president is serious about meeting the unmet promise of guaranteed healthcare in this county, I’m ready to work alongside leaders in the Senate to deliver. President Trump, give me a call! I’m happy to chat. Let’s get this done for the American people. Abdul Before you go... Senator-Elect Abdul El-Sayed is heading to the U.S. Senate to champion Medicare for All. It’s a moral and economic imperative. And we know he’ll fight for universal health care without an ounce of the corrupting influence from Big Pharma, health insurance companies, or other big money interests. Because from the very beginning, Abdul’s campaign was funded exclusively by people like YOU. No corporate PACs. [ ]Our grassroots money is our power. name: Rep. Ilhan Omar
subject: Let me explain? →
body:
Peter, let me
explain my dilemma.

Trump and his team have talked about having DHS go after me for months,
and now they’ve made it official.

DHS agents showed up at my doorstep and raided my home. Now we’ve gone
from words to actions, and my team is preparing for the long legal battle
that may come next as we prove to the American people that this
investigation is entirely a partisan delusion.

But this is a tactic Trump’s used for years now. Take people to court,
even when you know you can’t win, to drain their time and resources.

And I’m going to be honest, I’m not a billionaire like Donald Trump and
his buddies. I’m preparing to pay immense legal fees to be able to take on
this investigation, and it’s going to be expensive.

So, I’m coming to this team today to humbly ask for help.

If you can chip in $10 today, it would go a long way. That’s because it’s
not just your $10,
Peter.

There are thousands, if not millions, of Americans who oppose Trump’s
authoritarian agenda and stand with me and this entire movement. If
everybody chips in just a little bit, we can raise the money we need to
cover any legal fees that come our way and go on offense against MAGA.
What do you say?

the Squad Victory Fund to help me take on Trump’s corrupt abuse of power?
We are going to fight this ridiculous investigation, and with your help,
we are going to win.

[ https://act.squadvictoryfund.com/go/19213?c0=svfem-20261123-movement-split.3_3-Cb&refcode=em20261123-2977&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1020&akid=2977%2E342411%2EZij4Ko ]Contribute ››

In solidarity today and always,

Rep. Ilhan Omar

name: Josh Shapiro
subject: The status quo
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY SHAPIRO FOR PENNSYLVANIA]
body:
[ stdin# ]Josh Shapiro for Pennsylvania
For too many families, it feels like the game is fixed before it even
starts. That’s the status quo Americans are living in right now — thanks
to far-right politicians in DC, and even here in Pennsylvania.

But Derek, voters
rejected that status quo on November 3rd. In the loudest, boldest, most
outspoken way possible.

This moment calls for more than tinkering with tax codes, patching up
safety nets, or throwing money at problems. We need big, new, bold ideas —
and a willingness to fight for them to the end. [ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/23988?t=1001&akid=973%2E245147%2Eu9qZpz ]But here in the most
competitive battleground state in the country, no fight is won easily. So
please, chip in just $5 to help us turn as many of those big, new, bold
ideas into reality as we possibly can under our brand-new Democratic
trifecta.

[ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/23988?t=1002&akid=973%2E245147%2Eu9qZpz ]Donate →

Trust me, Derek: We
haven’t accomplished everything I would’ve liked over the last four years.
MAGA Republicans, time and time again, stood directly in the way of our
progress.

But despite those roadblocks, we showed voters that we’re willing to shake
up the status quo — and on Election Day, voters overwhelmingly chose that
path forward.

When a section of I-95 collapsed in Philly, we rebuilt it in twelve days.
Not twelve months.

When the pundits told us free school breakfast was impossible in a swing
state like Pennsylvania, we got it done.

And when Republicans continued to block an increase to Pennsylvania’s
minimum wage? We didn’t sit on our hands and give up. We fought. We
organized. And we ended the GOP’s majority in the Pennsylvania Senate —
delivering a historic Democratic trifecta for the first time in three
decades.

[ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/23988?t=1003&akid=973%2E245147%2Eu9qZpz ]Hard work. Big ideas. More fights. That’s what the American people
voted for on November 3rd — and Derek,
it’s the kind of government I’m going to
continue to lead as your Governor. If you’re with me, please, chip in $5
or whatever you can to help us keep rejecting the tired status quo — and
build something new here in Pennsylvania and all across the country.

If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your
donation will go through immediately:

[ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/23989?t=1004&akid=973%2E245147%2Eu9qZpz ]Donate $5 →

Thank you,

Josh Shapiro

name: Nico, United We Dream
subject: They tried to make us afraid. We chose to build leaders.🧡
body:
Join us on December 9 to celebrate! | | | Hi Peter, **They tried to make us afraid. We chose to build leaders.** 🧡 In a year marked by intensified immigration enforcement, deportations, and attacks on immigrant communities, young people across the country refused to let fear define their future. Instead, **they came together to learn, organize, and build the power to protect their communities**. Through our **People Power East and West convenings** , immigrant youth from across the country gathered to develop the skills, strategies, and relationships needed to lead campaigns on their campuses and in their communities. [](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.XaF8mXqsA6b2dSPmhsleMchKqTlnDL9HV9V-hz_r8qN5sFN7uyIDHDQ_kqfTbgHpzQ4lajrQE0IJPVPEzAEyztyuM0o9LFshHvmWysI4l73X5cvLDCCzW3jNKR9NdIjtcPNmM8nRMZvtRk-MERqBj2LuRB1_cZfNqEeDCYXDWCjSZheOFNro0sYCWZADO6L7m2a1PaZX7ejwpARzGvkOTNbjaD0gZja8VHVxDcMxwEzTIxFZVOuHW30aq7LuADserqpEcP92qLmQJYBpe-l8hJCNxmmeUTPe_zEIqr2mi5DQYcrD8yk8APiF8xBunFJC/4vz/eJsbYkUMQo-xhE4oaMMdfQ/h0/h001.1zWqeah6z0HUCJv7u2DbYOT6zu2gSkgC7voGphuOToE) Over 70 students from more than 25 schools across the country came together to plan their Powered by Students campaigns, working to protect access to higher education, defend in-state tuition, and build safer campuses for everyone, regardless of immigration status. **Our leaders learned about organizing, developed campaign plans, practiced building strategies, and connected with other young people fighting for the same future.** [](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.XaF8mXqsA6b2dSPmhsleMchKqTlnDL9HV9V-hz_r8qN5sFN7uyIDHDQ_kqfTbgHpzQ4lajrQE0IJPVPEzAEyztyuM0o9LFshHvmWysI4l733VsOBGAlv6TZRkZKQcfvM-IL16VwhkPFlStHIYAkFlwCkth7Jus-rdB7ToMzG8rPwciRM6YG2jzX78VTWGafPLTC7Dohw7Z9oEocNJBEQgGmXIlw1sBFrkFf4aex9m-VXJHRj9vp29C0ORbfzdP9Ct_eqNByDkf9PA8UwIuCO6QWcmg4Hey0-E8yw15YM-0AyelJw9BqOfxgCnsPofZei/4vz/eJsbYkUMQo-xhE4oaMMdfQ/h1/h001.-HUnR8qzukxHSh3nrJFOuO7D081KOIMEXLFPU6m3fVY) As one student reflected: _"The most impactful part is definitely all of the knowledge I’ve gained and strategies I'm able to take back to my campus. Also, the knowledge of having such a diverse group fighting for the same goals all across the country together will forever be so inspiring!"_ **This is what people power looks like.** When our communities needed courage, we created spaces where young people could discover their own. And now, we want to celebrate the people making it possible! **[🎉 Join us for Powered by You, our end-of-year Community Call, on Wednesday, December 9 at 7 PM ET!](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.XaF8mXqsA6b2dSPmhsleMchKqTlnDL9HV9V-hz_r8qN5sFN7uyIDHDQ_kqfTbgHpzQ4lajrQE0IJPVPEzAEyztyuM0o9LFshHvmWysI4l72ZfqEtdBpxL5vtunP9kiq4FOl_Y4zhBB4fGA3kixEhyjaETC5NUo9wccJYF13yDg8dwO3Vm1un1hq3cDMBMeoOurGLm4NG75yAxHmBRZ17d_dHJ7b8EYRJiQMTvvsrpYE3f52mDK42sywM3gi7464DIwZn8ww79F_aZ_LRMEAVz0ubUvHEmD1fxKoNmEzxnI9wuzHlJoiDT56OSRF9GoXP/4vz/eJsbYkUMQo-xhE4oaMMdfQ/h2/h001.sP7pVUqzu58Rnn7QWuwgq3mtfWK9mcMLZ4p-kEQFVNU)** [](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.XaF8mXqsA6b2dSPmhsleMchKqTlnDL9HV9V-hz_r8qN5sFN7uyIDHDQ_kqfTbgHpzQ4lajrQE0IJPVPEzAEyztyuM0o9LFshHvmWysI4l72xWMxGbeyEvOwrDMM8GGRtMafJ4vz3KF8yGu7pMVAcriLRAKWOzhhXDrgalZfcWDubUGanyl48BE4grj6MkFWwa7gwHHQKgYLonRrvTMoUHlPbIRdhy1b5eQomWSXavrFAPy5cZSyPu9TnxiNXX8aDcnbhyXkcpRdQBJPT67aP14CVX3-8tbSXjtndujv-vqdM5AxNy0YMBDpLCPFvgHbD/4vz/eJsbYkUMQo-xhE4oaMMdfQ/h3/h001.qnw4HiLBIXfu6r3Fj9i7txb48oPrnSnJ75hAcoTUa_Y) We'll come together to celebrate the young people building the future of our movement, reflect on what our communities accomplished this year, and look ahead to what's possible when we continue organizing together. | | [RSVP HERE](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.XaF8mXqsA6b2dSPmhsleMchKqTlnDL9HV9V-hz_r8qN5sFN7uyIDHDQ_kqfTbgHpzQ4lajrQE0IJPVPEzAEyztyuM0o9LFshHvmWysI4l72HIzo6INOnQuxhX7QkkrMb9rmm1WTEPcpoZnEWBToYUO2nug0wIELRTqFGURQt7uLzWTmYFo7ouwkeiNHendN_nkNXjUD7jbD43QbxzaTRda78br5Y8Vkt4X7T7dB0nKhuU6-fVWezvpxYiYRVYFBBiDYryfs1GamfoFyOmarbKewTup2s-Wc34OziHu6MUqi432fn2yj4vlmQa78HFkvf/4vz/eJsbYkUMQo-xhE4oaMMdfQ/h4/h001.H4f_UXJ2pZSaVvjmQ_vd6DXEfntQWhvDUyBVKn2n328)

clean_body: Join us on December 9 to celebrate! | | | Hi Peter, They tried to make us afraid. We chose to build leaders. 🧡 In a year marked by intensified immigration enforcement, deportations, and attacks on immigrant communities, young people across the country refused to let fear define their future. Instead, they came together to learn, organize, and build the power to protect their communities. Through our People Power East and West convenings , immigrant youth from across the country gathered to develop the skills, strategies, and relationships needed to lead campaigns on their campuses and in their communities. Over 70 students from more than 25 schools across the country came together to plan their Powered by Students campaigns, working to protect access to higher education, defend in-state tuition, and build safer campuses for everyone, regardless of immigration status. Our leaders learned about organizing, developed campaign plans, practiced building strategies, and connected with other young people fighting for the same future. As one student reflected: "The most impactful part is definitely all of the knowledge I’ve gained and strategies I'm able to take back to my campus. Also, the knowledge of having such a diverse group fighting for the same goals all across the country together will forever be so inspiring!" This is what people power looks like. When our communities needed courage, we created spaces where young people could discover their own. And now, we want to celebrate the people making it possible! We'll come together to celebrate the young people building the future of our movement, reflect on what our communities accomplished this year, and look ahead to what's possible when we continue organizing together. | | We are building the future of our movement, right here, right now, with young people who know that change starts with us. ✊🏽 We hope to see you there! In solidarity, Nico and the United We Dream Team 🧡 Follow us on: | | | | |

| | |

_Measles elimination status terminated. Nationwide foodborne illness outbreaks. Plummeting confidence in proven science. Double-digit health care premium hikes. Millions of lives on the line._

Look, Peter: President Trump and RFK Jr. have put our public health system on life support.

We can’t just rebuild what they’ve torn down – we have to make it too strong to be broken by anti-science political interference ever again.

**And it starts with RFK Jr. either being fired or resigning immediately.** **[_If you agree, join me in calling for his immediate termination (or resignation) by signing my petition now._](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/143942273/661893399/886426107?email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&ask=5&refcode=jtk725-su-nd&code=jtk725-su-nd&recurring=0&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS85MDM4NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI1ZjUwZWM1Yi04YmU3LWYxMTEtOTFmMy0wMDBkM2E1MzM5NzgiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=biFDHksD4x9hdhEjJEAcSWBhmxKBSOhhAD3G2fPO5tg=&emci=36b96102-10e5-f111-91f3-000d3a533978&emdi=5f50ec5b-8be7-f111-91f3-000d3a533978&ceid=13116610)**

Amid real public health crises, RFK Jr. is abusing his authority to act on truly insane conspiracy theories and disinformation – and we’re seeing the consequences in real time. He’s making Americans less healthy and people are dying.

But since Senate Democrats won’t have the numbers to make him answer for his disastrous tenure until January, we’ve got to keep up the pressure on Trump to do the right thing for once in his life and finally tell RFK Jr., _“You’re FIRED.”_

[**_So even if you’ve signed this petition before, Peter, I need as many folks standing with me for as long as it takes to get this anti-vaxxer conspiracy theorist out as the nation’s top public health official. Will you please be one of the 30,000 folks I need to speak out with me before 11:59 p.m. tonight and demand RFK Jr.’s dismissal?_**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/143942274/661893400/886426107?email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&ask=5&refcode=jtk725-su-nd&code=jtk725-su-nd&recurring=0&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS85MDM4NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI1ZjUwZWM1Yi04YmU3LWYxMTEtOTFmMy0wMDBkM2E1MzM5NzgiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=biFDHksD4x9hdhEjJEAcSWBhmxKBSOhhAD3G2fPO5tg=&emci=36b96102-10e5-f111-91f3-000d3a533978&emdi=5f50ec5b-8be7-f111-91f3-000d3a533978&ceid=13116610)

Something once unthinkable is happening in Washington: Donald Trump is asking Democrats to help him cap credit card interest rates at roughly 10 percent, and Elizabeth Warren is saying yes. When Trump, Warren, Bernie Sanders, Josh Hawley, AOC and Republican congresswoman Anna Paulina Luna all land on the same side of an issue, you should ask what the banks did to deserve it. The answer is that they spent five decades converting the credit card into a legal loan-shark operation, and the Federal Reserve supervised the whole thing from the front row.
Do the math. The 30-year Treasury -- the government's longest, most certain IOU -- hovers around 5 percent. Freddie Mac put the 30-year mortgage at 7.11 percent on November 12. A mortgage is money lent against your house: documented, underwritten, collateralized, recourse if you default. Meanwhile, the Fed's own G.19 release puts the average credit card rate at 21.2 percent across all accounts, 22.4 percent on cards actually carrying a balance, and Forbes Advisor's weekly tally runs 24.9 percent. Penalty rates touch 30. Your bank can borrow from the Fed's discount window today at 4.00 percent flat. It borrows at 4, lends secured at 7, and lends unsecured at 22 to 29 -- to the same customers, in the same week, sometimes on the same screen.
Nothing about the word "unsecured" explains an eighteen-point spread. What explains it is fifty years of regulatory negligence.
How we got here. Before 1978, every state had usury laws -- ceilings of roughly 10 to 12 percent that applied to even the riskiest consumer money. Then came '**Marquette National Bank v. First of Omaha** ', in which the Supreme Court ruled that a bank could charge its home state's rate to customers in any state. Within two years, South Dakota repealed its cap to lure Citibank's card operation; Delaware did the same for the rest of the industry. Overnight, the national ceiling vanished. Credit card lending moved to whichever state would take the bribe.
The Federal Reserve watched this happen and chose disclosure over protection. Truth in Lending gave borrowers fine print instead of price limits. The banks' next innovation was the 0 percent teaser: twelve to eighteen months of free balance transfers, pitched as generosity, engineered as bait -- the monthly cadence that conditions you to carry a balance just before the "go-to" rate of 25 to 29.99 percent kicks in. The CARD Act of 2009 finally banned retroactive rate hikes and surprise fees, and cardholders have been materially better off for it -- but it never touched the price of the money itself. On the Fed's numbers, the average rate charged on balances that accrue interest nearly doubled from 12.9 percent in late 2013 to 22.8 percent in 2023, the highest since the Fed began collecting the data in 1994. The CFPB has called card interest rate margins an all-time high -- and that was before this decade of rate hikes was fully repriced.
The scale. The CFPB tallied the industry's interest revenue at $105 billion in a single year, plus another $25 billion in fees -- and the bulk of both comes from cardholders with lower credit scores. That is the definition of a regressive tax: the people with the least pay the most, at rates no state legislature would have approved in 1977.
The industry's defense is risk-based pricing: unsecured revolving debt defaults more than mortgages, so it must cost more; cap it at 10 percent and rewards programs die, subprime borrowers lose access, and credit gets rationed. Studies -- some Vanderbilt's, many industry-funded -- warn of exactly that. There is a fair point buried in there: nobody serious says unsecured money should price like a Treasury. But run the numbers. Mortgage and card charge-offs are both running in normal single digits, while card margins have _doubled_ to a record. That is not a risk premium; that is market power, compounded by a Fed that set the prime rate, published the G.19 showing the margin widening, and never once said aloud what its own data showed. Usury ceilings coexisted with abundant consumer credit for centuries. If 10 percent is genuinely too low to price a risky borrower, write the cap at 15 and underwrite honestly -- but do not tell me that 29.99 percent plus a $40 late fee is prudence rather than the vig.
Where it stands. Sanders and Hawley's bill (**S. 381**) caps card rates at 10 percent for five years; AOC and Luna carry it in the House; Trump wants his name on it, and the banking committee's incoming chairwoman wants hers next to his. Whatever number survives committee -- 10, 15, somewhere between -- the argument Trump has opened is the one the Federal Reserve should have forced decades ago, back when the first teaser offers taught America that 22 percent was normal.
A 22 percent rate on money the same banks extend at 7 percent against a house isn't risk pricing, and it isn't financial innovation. It's loan sharking with a rewards program and a mobile app. Half a century of regulators pretending otherwise is why a Republican president and democratic socialists finally agree.
Sources: Freddie Mac PMMS (Nov. 12, 2026); Federal Reserve G.19 Consumer Credit; Federal Reserve H.15; Forbes Advisor weekly rate report (Nov. 9, 2026); CFPB, "Credit card interest rate margins at all-time high"; S. 381 (Sanders-Hawley, 2025).

body:
That question is whether the Second and Fourteenth Amendments guarantee the right to possess AR-15s and similar semiautomatic rifles — commonly known as assault weapons.
#

Team,
In just a few days, the Supreme Court is going to consider a question that will shape the movement to end gun violence for years to come.
That question is whether the Second and Fourteenth Amendments guarantee the right to possess AR-15s and similar semiautomatic rifles — commonly known as assault weapons.
In 2022, the Supreme Court created a loose standard to assess regulations on gun safety. If state or federal gun safety legislation comes before the Supreme Court, the defenders of those laws have to prove that they fit within a “tradition” of firearms regulation in the United States. They have to point to historical analogs that similarly regulated firearms for the laws in question to be considered constitutional.
Now, here’s the tough truth: We don’t have any control over how the Supreme Court is going to rule in this case. But GIFFORDS is one of the few organizations in the country positioned to do something about it, no matter what the justices decide.
GIFFORDS has helped pass more than 900 lifesaving gun safety regulations around the country since our founding nearly 14 years ago. And whatever happens in this case, we know we are going to need our team of grassroots supporters with us.
That’s how we’ve helped make historic gains in courtrooms, state legislatures, and Congress. That’s how we’ve elected countless gun safety champions over the years. And with your help, that’s how we’ll continue this fight and do everything we can to save lives in the years ahead.

body:
# [](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/43706?t=1&akid=241188%2E444211%2ErsIM1O)
Did you see this article highlighting our work in _The Nation_?
[](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/68300?t=3&akid=241188%2E444211%2ErsIM1O)
**Here’s a quick excerpt.[You can click here to read the full article.](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/68300?t=4&akid=241188%2E444211%2ErsIM1O)**
> “O’Rourke described Powered by People’s organizing strategy as one centered on maintaining personal contact with voters. Rather than passing newly registered voters’ information to a campaign or political party, volunteers ask permission to stay in touch directly, he said. They help students determine what identification they need, locate polling places, and make plans to vote.
> ‘I’ve been on the road every single week of this semester and every week of the last semester,’ O’Rourke said. ‘I’m there to answer students’ questions, to engage in conversations,’ he added.”
There are a lot of headlines right now saying things along the lines of “Texas flipped Blue” and we appreciate them. But we have never believed that Texas was a “Red” or “Blue” state but rather a state that the establishment had written off. Leaving people feeling that their vote didn’t matter.
Beto started Powered by People in 2019 after he lost to Ted Cruz by less than 3%. In that campaign he went to all 254 counties to meet with and listen to Texans who all too often were left behind or taken for granted.
We brought that "leave no one behind" belief from Beto’s Senate campaign to Powered by People, and as you know, it paid off big time this year.
You already know that Gina Hinojosa and James Talarico won their statewide campaigns — an incredible feat. But also, we organized in 12 Texas House races, including nine seats Republicans held that Democrats have now won. In those districts, three in four voters in our network cast a ballot.
This is the work that works. Thank you for being a part of it.
More soon,
Team PxP
One more thing before you click away...
Powered by People volunteers and organizers go where young Texans are: college campuses, coffee shops, and concerts to register Texans to vote. Then we personally stay in touch with them to answer questions, help them make a plan to vote, and continue to encourage them 1:1 until we can confirm that they’ve voted.
[**If you can afford it, chip in today to support the work our organizers and volunteers are doing each and every day to register new voters in Texas. We’re in this work for the long haul.**](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/56109?c0=pbp-em-20261123.IjxPVA&refcode=ema20261123-241188&t=5&akid=241188%2E444211%2ErsIM1O)

subject: The producer of Sound of Freedom has a message for you
body:
One little girl cried out for help. Someone listened. Now she's safe.

| | | |
---
| |
---
| | God's Children Are Not For Sale
---
|
---
| | | Friend,
---
Have you ever heard a sound you just couldn't ignore?

For one woman staying in a hotel, it was the scream of a little girl on the other side of the wall.

I want to introduce you to "Daisy."

But that's not her real name. We'll call her Daisy to protect her privacy.

And her story is why I am writing to you today.

My name is Eduardo Verastegui. I am the producer of the film _Sound of Freedom_ and the new movie _Zero A.D_.: The Birth of Christ, which hits theaters in December.

Years ago, I met rescuers who told me what really happens to children who are trafficked.

It broke my heart.

And it left me with a question I still can't shake...

_What if it were my child_?
---
[ Rescue a Child -- Give Now](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJycUTtvpDAQ_jWmW4QfGChcnA6tdMVue6U12ANYhzFnG6L8-4glRYpU6ebxPebT_H3oB7jFrdMTPCpzOB2TzjNuMdjdYAxjCvtqwzhGRKtZxeSN0hvjGkx2B2oBhVXGSs4KVLTpatGIlrbFrJq2Ni1S7CwbjbBDN1A5dEwAbZuxxqpw6pSjlHHGq4rWJdCuEbaWg0FroGuJqPbNQsZUmrAmjAecnm5dw1mFtTTBF4uac94S4b8IuxN2T2j2iOXXu4Mfz-7ihDidqDBqCy69vzJpMP8Jv6ewR4PaBIuE97__PKnkUraEyT177dG63RPeowe3fA4vCuH9DNFC-vdSulYG_AZuWgnvv3G7MBnjqVhEZbc3tywuyYaIajodXunyD59yKPYRAAD__xr7oVg)
---
Hollywood said Sound of Freedom would never succeed.

Doors closed. Studios walked away.

**But we refused to give up. **

Because **God 's children are not for sale.**

After the film, I started **Sound of Freedom Foundation** to keep that fight going, long after the credits roll.

Let me show you what that fight looks like.
---
[](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJycUTtvpDAQ_jWmW4QfGChcnA6tdMVue6U12ANYhzFnG6L8-4glRYpU6ebxPebT_H3oB7jFrdMTPCpzOB2TzjNuMdjdYAxjCvtqwzhGRKtZxeSN0hvjGkx2B2oBhVXGSs4KVLTpatGIlrbFrJq2Ni1S7CwbjbBDN1A5dEwAbZuxxqpw6pSjlHHGq4rWJdCuEbaWg0FroGuJqPbNQsZUmrAmjAecnm5dw1mFtTTBF4uac94S4b8IuxN2T2j2iOXXu4Mfz-7ihDidqDBqCy69vzJpMP8Jv6ewR4PaBIuE97__PKnkUraEyT177dG63RPeowe3fA4vCuH9DNFC-vdSulYG_AZuWgnvv3G7MBnjqVhEZbc3tywuyYaIajodXunyD59yKPYRAAD__xr7oVg)
---
[ Rescue a Child -- Give Now](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJycUTtvpDAQ_jWmW4QfGChcnA6tdMVue6U12ANYhzFnG6L8-4glRYpU6ebxPebT_H3oB7jFrdMTPCpzOB2TzjNuMdjdYAxjCvtqwzhGRKtZxeSN0hvjGkx2B2oBhVXGSs4KVLTpatGIlrbFrJq2Ni1S7CwbjbBDN1A5dEwAbZuxxqpw6pSjlHHGq4rWJdCuEbaWg0FroGuJqPbNQsZUmrAmjAecnm5dw1mFtTTBF4uac94S4b8IuxN2T2j2iOXXu4Mfz-7ihDidqDBqCy69vzJpMP8Jv6ewR4PaBIuE97__PKnkUraEyT177dG63RPeowe3fA4vCuH9DNFC-vdSulYG_AZuWgnvv3G7MBnjqVhEZbc3tywuyYaIajodXunyD59yKPYRAAD__xr7oVg)
---
Daisy was only ten years old when her own older sister sold her to a trafficker.

She was forced into a taxi and taken to a hotel, where a grown man was waiting to hurt her.

But Daisy fought back. She screamed as loud as she could.

**And the woman next door heard her.**

She tried to get inside. When she couldn't, she ran to the front desk and demanded they call for help.

**Police came. The man was arrested. **

And Daisy was brought straight to one of our safe children's homes.

Friend, rescue is only the beginning.

Daisy came to us with wounds no child should ever carry.

For the next couple of years, she was surrounded by safety, love, counseling, and school.

And by people who reminded her every day:

_What happened to you does not define you. You are valuable. You are loved. You are God 's child. _

Then came the best day of all.

Daisy was placed with her forever family. Today, she is a beloved daughter with a safe home and a bright future.
---
[](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJycUTtvpDAQ_jWmW4QfGChcnA6tdMVue6U12ANYhzFnG6L8-4glRYpU6ebxPebT_H3oB7jFrdMTPCpzOB2TzjNuMdjdYAxjCvtqwzhGRKtZxeSN0hvjGkx2B2oBhVXGSs4KVLTpatGIlrbFrJq2Ni1S7CwbjbBDN1A5dEwAbZuxxqpw6pSjlHHGq4rWJdCuEbaWg0FroGuJqPbNQsZUmrAmjAecnm5dw1mFtTTBF4uac94S4b8IuxN2T2j2iOXXu4Mfz-7ihDidqDBqCy69vzJpMP8Jv6ewR4PaBIuE97__PKnkUraEyT177dG63RPeowe3fA4vCuH9DNFC-vdSulYG_AZuWgnvv3G7MBnjqVhEZbc3tywuyYaIajodXunyD59yKPYRAAD__xr7oVg)
---
That is what **Sound of Freedom Foundatio** n does. **Rescue. Restore. Raise.**
---
* We help **rescue** children by equipping the brave agents and partners who find them.
* We **restore** survivors with a safe place to heal -- body, mind, and soul.
* We help **raise** them in loving families, so they can grow up free.

---
And we work to stop trafficking before it starts, by helping struggling families and teaching parents the warning signs.
---
[ Rescue a Child -- Give Now](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJycUTtvpDAQ_jWmW4QfGChcnA6tdMVue6U12ANYhzFnG6L8-4glRYpU6ebxPebT_H3oB7jFrdMTPCpzOB2TzjNuMdjdYAxjCvtqwzhGRKtZxeSN0hvjGkx2B2oBhVXGSs4KVLTpatGIlrbFrJq2Ni1S7CwbjbBDN1A5dEwAbZuxxqpw6pSjlHHGq4rWJdCuEbaWg0FroGuJqPbNQsZUmrAmjAecnm5dw1mFtTTBF4uac94S4b8IuxN2T2j2iOXXu4Mfz-7ihDidqDBqCy69vzJpMP8Jv6ewR4PaBIuE97__PKnkUraEyT177dG63RPeowe3fA4vCuH9DNFC-vdSulYG_AZuWgnvv3G7MBnjqVhEZbc3tywuyYaIajodXunyD59yKPYRAAD__xr7oVg)
---
Jesus said, "_Let the little children come to me, and do not hinder them, for the kingdom of heaven belongs to such as these._ " (Matthew 19:14, NIV)

**Every child is precious to God.** And I believe He calls us to protect them.

Here is the hard truth, Friend ...

Human trafficking cases have been reported in all 50 U.S. states. And tonight, another child is crying out behind a locked door.

The woman next door could not open that door by herself. But she made sure help came.

**You can do the same thing today.**

Will you make your first gift to **Sound of Freedom Foundation**?

**[Will you give $25, $50, $75, $100, or whatever you can right now to help rescue, restore, and raise more children like Daisy?](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJycUTtvpDAQ_jWmW4QfGChcnA6tdMVue6U12ANYhzFnG6L8-4glRYpU6ebxPebT_H3oB7jFrdMTPCpzOB2TzjNuMdjdYAxjCvtqwzhGRKtZxeSN0hvjGkx2B2oBhVXGSs4KVLTpatGIlrbFrJq2Ni1S7CwbjbBDN1A5dEwAbZuxxqpw6pSjlHHGq4rWJdCuEbaWg0FroGuJqPbNQsZUmrAmjAecnm5dw1mFtTTBF4uac94S4b8IuxN2T2j2iOXXu4Mfz-7ihDidqDBqCy69vzJpMP8Jv6ewR4PaBIuE97__PKnkUraEyT177dG63RPeowe3fA4vCuH9DNFC-vdSulYG_AZuWgnvv3G7MBnjqVhEZbc3tywuyYaIajodXunyD59yKPYRAAD__xr7oVg)**

Your gift helps rescue children from trafficking, restore them with love and healing, and give them the chance to grow up in a safe, loving family.

I often say... _when good people keep quiet, they become part of the problem. _

**Please don 't stay quiet. **

**Join us today.**

**God 's children are not for sale. **

Here’s the truth: working-class folks are having to pinch pennies because of Trump’s failed policies.

I know what it’s like to compare your paycheck and your bills and know there will be nothing left over. And frankly, I remember times when an $89 suit would have broken the bank for me and my family.

Mainers deserve better. They deserve quality, accessible healthcare, affordable housing, and to do more than just survive.

That’s what I am fighting for in the US Senate: Medicare for All, lowering the cost of prescription drugs, and affordable housing.

* * *
When I wrote **["Where the Hell Are the Republicans We Elected?"](https://substack.com/redirect/fe34577e-ca93-4a6f-a51f-ec9531755726?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** I didn't think I could be more angry or disgusted with them. Apparently, I underestimated their determination to earn it.
Hand Republicans power, and somehow they find a way to make you regret trusting them with it. Then, when the failure costs them an election, some cannot even be bothered to show up and finish their terms. We are still paying them. Leadership has to chase them down to vote.
You have got to be kidding me.
### **We the People Employ You**
CNN **[reported](https://substack.com/redirect/99dfcc71-62b8-40da-81f8-259d51df1bec?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** November 20 that Republican leaders were struggling to get some defeated members back to Washington to vote. Rep. Greg Murphy, who also lost his seat, was there doing his job. "If they aren't here, they shouldn't get paid," he said.
### **Get your ass back to work**
Your constituents are still entitled to representation. Your salary certainly did not stop when the returns came in. You do not get to sulk through the remainder of your term because voters declined to renew your contract.
You wanted that office badly enough to ask people for money, knock on their doors, and interrupt their dinners with campaign calls. Finish the damn work.
These pompous children learned nothing. After a defeat that should have prompted serious examination of their performance, some apparently decided the appropriate response was to make leadership chase them down for votes. Imagine explaining to your employer that you were too disappointed about losing your job in January to perform the job you still have in November.

### **And Now, Thanksgiving Recess**
Both chambers are scheduled to **[return November 30.](https://substack.com/redirect/a6bbe215-7aa2-45e6-b53d-f5c3554ffd90?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** The Senate has brief pro forma sessions during the break, but regular floor business is paused while unfinished priorities wait.
Ask the American people how much paid time off they get. Ask how many can take a week away **[while important work sits unfinished](https://substack.com/redirect/5bd8700c-6ace-49e9-a20e-f81527509d5e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**. Ask the nurse working twelve hours on Thanksgiving, the police officer answering calls while his family eats without him, or the firefighter whose dinner gets cold when the alarm sounds.
Ask the hotel housekeeper cleaning up after someone else's holiday. Ask the grocery clerk working the register and the truck driver delivering what everyone else will put on the table. Ask the waitress bringing your pumpkin pie whether she gets to go home and have some with her children.
If she can finish her shift, you overpaid, self-important cowards can finish your damn terms.
Let them gorge themselves on turkey and pumpkin pie as if they have accomplished something worthy of celebration. I hope someone at the table asks what they intend to accomplish when they return. Perhaps a relative could ask the questions their consultants would prefer everyone avoid.
Leadership could have sought additional legislative days. Staying in Washington would not guarantee passage of a bill, but it would provide more time to negotiate and make decisions while Republicans still control both chambers. If leadership believed that time would accomplish nothing, explain why.
They spent the campaign telling Americans the country could not wait. I would like to know why their schedules could.
### **What Happened to the SAVE Act?**
The House **[passed the SAVE Act](https://substack.com/redirect/8294d6c3-c3d5-44e7-844f-f2dab982a212?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** in April 2025 and the expanded SAVE America Act in February 2026. Neither became law before the midterms. The Senate's legislative listing still shows the SAVE America Act without an enacted public-law citation.
Republicans retain a legislative window before the new Congress begins January 3. Losing an election does not immediately transfer their authority to the incoming Democrats.
Could they pass it before then? There is still time. But they would have to secure additional support, negotiate an agreement, or muster the votes for a change in Senate precedent.
Under ordinary Senate procedures, overcoming a legislative filibuster generally requires 60 votes. Final passage usually requires a simple majority. Having enough votes to pass a bill does not necessarily mean having enough votes to end debate and reach that vote.
I understand the distinction. So did leadership when it made the promises.
What I want to know is what they intend to do about it.

# **We 're not giving up this fight, and neither should you**
The midterms were a wake up call to all American patriots...
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/1a0f868c-d673-4433-875c-ffbb0792f853?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

### **Show Us the Actual Strategy**
Negotiation is one option. What provisions could attract enough additional support? What changes would leadership consider, and would the resulting agreement still accomplish the legislation's central purpose?
Another option is pursuing a change in Senate precedent to create **[a filibuster exception.](https://substack.com/redirect/deb31000-cb8e-4f63-94af-815fae8edf81?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** That requires a sufficiently united majority willing to support the procedural change. If Republicans lack that support within their own conference, explain who objects and why.
They could also seek to attach provisions to spending, defense, or another bill with broader support. That creates negotiating leverage. It does not automatically eliminate the Senate's procedural requirements, and leadership would have to decide what it was willing to risk if the larger bill stalled.
Then there is budget reconciliation, so often presented as Washington's magical escape hatch. It has limits. **[The Byrd Rule](https://substack.com/redirect/c7258742-7226-479b-a293-0527cb79d9e3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** restricts provisions that have no budgetary effect or whose budgetary effects are merely incidental to their policy purpose. Waiving a Byrd Rule objection normally requires 60 votes. Calling election policy a budget measure does not automatically make it eligible.
Those are real obstacles. They were also known before the election.
Which route is leadership pursuing? Which has it ruled out? What can realistically be accomplished before January 3?
If the votes cannot be secured, say so. Explain what was attempted, what concessions were considered, and why the effort failed. Americans can understand an honest explanation. They should not have to extract it from the people who spent months asking for their trust.
And be honest about what legislation passed now would do. It would apply according to its effective dates and implementation requirements. It would not retroactively impose new requirements on ballots already cast in November. Questions about the election that occurred require records, audits, and investigations under the applicable law.
Republicans should be able to explain that distinction without confusing supporters or exploiting their frustration.
### **There Is a Constitutional Fight, Too**
Noncitizen voting in federal elections is already prohibited under **[18 U.S.C.§ 611,](https://substack.com/redirect/4ff25e0b-4b3e-4e8d-98db-19002c5520eb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** subject to the statute's exceptions. But a recent ruling raises a separate question about federal enforcement.
On October 1, U.S. District Judge David Leibowitz **[dismissed the federal noncitizen-voting charge](https://substack.com/redirect/fa5acaf1-370b-4f91-ab72-98e52f16d099?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** against Chelsea Cox in Florida. He held the statute unconstitutional as applied to her, reasoning that Congress had exceeded its authority by establishing a voter qualification reserved to the states.
The judge did not legalize noncitizen voting nationwide. His ruling addressed Cox's prosecution, and he expressly recognized that Florida could prohibit and punish the alleged conduct under state law. The federal government filed its **[notice of appeal](https://substack.com/redirect/42f2fbac-acb9-4ff3-ad25-2b98b54af0f0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** October 2.
The order also distinguished the existing statute from a potential federal enforcement law supporting a state's own prohibition on noncitizen voting. The judge did not decide whether such legislation would survive. He identified a different approach that Congress could examine.
Has Republican leadership examined it? Requested a legislative analysis? Explained whether a response is warranted alongside the government's appeal?
This does not establish that SAVE would cure the constitutional issue. It does mean that repeating "it is already illegal" does not fully answer a dispute about who can prosecute the conduct and under what authority.
Congress has lawyers, committees, and legislative counsel. Put them to work.
Voters should not have to research the problem and then beg elected officials to read it.

## **I Feel Used. I Doubt I 'm Alone.**
I have spent more than twenty years building and leading companies. Obstacles come with the job. You identify them, decide how to address them, and change course when the approach fails. You also answer for the outcome. Nobody meeting payroll gets to spend indefinitely explaining why the business environment was difficult.
Yet voters are expected to accept precisely that from people who sought the authority to govern the country. We are supposed to absorb the disappointment, defend the party, and prepare to contribute again. Another emergency appeal will arrive soon enough, explaining why everything depends on what we do next. I would appreciate an accounting of what they did first.
That is why I feel manipulated. The sacrifice always seems to flow in one direction. Ordinary Americans spend money they could use for their families and risk relationships defending people who become remarkably cautious when their own political capital is at stake.
I am sick of Republicans campaigning like warriors and governing like they are afraid to offend the furniture.
I do not expect them to win every fight. I expect them to prepare, know the rules, develop a strategy, and show up. When the strategy fails, explain what happened without treating the question as an act of betrayal. Supporting a party does not obligate anyone to excuse incompetence.
## **Why Would Good People Want This Job?**
I understand why capable people might look at public office and decide their families have endured enough without volunteering for that circus. Their spouses and children become targets, their finances are scrutinized, and every old remark becomes ammunition. Then they watch people spend decades in Washington explaining why the work could not be done.
What an extraordinary recruiting pitch.
I worry about the people we lose before they ever consider running. People who have built something useful, managed a crisis, and accepted responsibility when their decisions went wrong. We need that experience, and voters need to make room for it.
Familiar names are not permanent entitlements to office. A Republican label does not establish competence, and an endorsement does not replace a record. Getting elected proves you won an election. What you do afterward determines whether you deserved the job.
## **You Still Owe Us**
When Congress returns, leadership should publish its agenda for the remaining weeks. Explain what it intends to pursue, where the votes stand, and what remains possible. Keep members present for votes and account for the results. If a promise cannot be delivered, have the courage to say so before asking supporters to finance the next one.
There should be shame in squandering an opportunity this consequential. There should be humiliation in asking the same voters for another dollar without explaining what happened to the mandate they already gave you.
You still hold office, still collect a salary, and still owe this country your work. I will respect a serious effort that falls short. I will not applaud people who abandon their responsibilities and expect gratitude for having held the title.
You lost your next term. You still owe us this one.
**Get your ass back to work. Your wounded pride is not a taxpayer obligation.**
