Then there is budget reconciliation, so often presented as Washington's magical escape hatch. It has limits. restricts provisions that have no budgetary effect or whose budgetary effects are merely incidental to their policy purpose. Waiving a Byrd Rule objection normally requires 60 votes. Calling election policy a budget measure does not automatically make it eligible. Those are real obstacles. They were also known before the election. Which route is leadership pursuing? Which has it ruled out? What can realistically be accomplished before January 3? If the votes cannot be secured, say so. Explain what was attempted, what concessions were considered, and why the effort failed. Americans can understand an honest explanation. They should not have to extract it from the people who spent months asking for their trust. And be honest about what legislation passed now would do. It would apply according to its effective dates and implementation requirements. It would not retroactively impose new requirements on ballots already cast in November. Questions about the election that occurred require records, audits, and investigations under the applicable law. Republicans should be able to explain that distinction without confusing supporters or exploiting their frustration. There Is a Constitutional Fight, Too Noncitizen voting in federal elections is already prohibited under subject to the statute's exceptions. But a recent ruling raises a separate question about federal enforcement. On October 1, U.S. District Judge David Leibowitz against Chelsea Cox in Florida. He held the statute unconstitutional as applied to her, reasoning that Congress had exceeded its authority by establishing a voter qualification reserved to the states. The judge did not legalize noncitizen voting nationwide. His ruling addressed Cox's prosecution, and he expressly recognized that Florida could prohibit and punish the alleged conduct under state law. The federal government filed its October 2. The order also distinguished the existing statute from a potential federal enforcement law supporting a state's own prohibition on noncitizen voting. The judge did not decide whether such legislation would survive. He identified a different approach that Congress could examine. Has Republican leadership examined it? Requested a legislative analysis? Explained whether a response is warranted alongside the government's appeal? This does not establish that SAVE would cure the constitutional issue. It does mean that repeating "it is already illegal" does not fully answer a dispute about who can prosecute the conduct and under what authority. Congress has lawyers, committees, and legislative counsel. Put them to work. Voters should not have to research the problem and then beg elected officials to read it. PolitiBrawl is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support our work, please consider becoming a paid subscriber. I Feel Used. I Doubt I 'm Alone. I have spent more than twenty years building and leading companies. Obstacles come with the job. You identify them, decide how to address them, and change course when the approach fails. You also answer for the outcome. Nobody meeting payroll gets to spend indefinitely explaining why the business environment was difficult. Yet voters are expected to accept precisely that from people who sought the authority to govern the country. We are supposed to absorb the disappointment, defend the party, and prepare to contribute again. Another emergency appeal will arrive soon enough, explaining why everything depends on what we do next. I would appreciate an accounting of what they did first. That is why I feel manipulated. The sacrifice always seems to flow in one direction. Ordinary Americans spend money they could use for their families and risk relationships defending people who become remarkably cautious when their own political capital is at stake. I am sick of Republicans campaigning like warriors and governing like they are afraid to offend the furniture. I do not expect them to win every fight. I expect them to prepare, know the rules, develop a strategy, and show up. When the strategy fails, explain what happened without treating the question as an act of betrayal. Supporting a party does not obligate anyone to excuse incompetence. Why Would Good People Want This Job? I understand why capable people might look at public office and decide their families have endured enough without volunteering for that circus. Their spouses and children become targets, their finances are scrutinized, and every old remark becomes ammunition. Then they watch people spend decades in Washington explaining why the work could not be done. What an extraordinary recruiting pitch. I worry about the people we lose before they ever consider running. People who have built something useful, managed a crisis, and accepted responsibility when their decisions went wrong. We need that experience, and voters need to make room for it. Familiar names are not permanent entitlements to office. A Republican label does not establish competence, and an endorsement does not replace a record. Getting elected proves you won an election. What you do afterward determines whether you deserved the job. You Still Owe Us When Congress returns, leadership should publish its agenda for the remaining weeks. Explain what it intends to pursue, where the votes stand, and what remains possible. Keep members present for votes and account for the results. If a promise cannot be delivered, have the courage to say so before asking supporters to finance the next one. There should be shame in squandering an opportunity this consequential. There should be humiliation in asking the same voters for another dollar without explaining what happened to the mandate they already gave you. You still hold office, still collect a salary, and still owe this country your work. I will respect a serious effort that falls short. I will not applaud people who abandon their responsibilities and expect gratitude for having held the title. You lost your next term. You still owe us this one. Get your ass back to work. Your wounded pride is not a taxpayer obligation. About the Author Wendy M. Yurgo is a Christ follower, mother, attorney, entrepreneur, and the Founder and CEO of Revere Payments, a conservative fintech company serving many of the nation's leading faith-based and freedom-driven organizations. She writes about where faith collides with the systems shaping our culture, bringing a legal and executive lens to the most urgent issues of our time. Patriot,

For more than five years, a group of January 6 Patriots, many of them veterans who served this country honorably, carried a weight most Americans can’t imagine: **politically charged trials, years behind bars, and a government that treated them like enemies of the state.**

President Trump commuted their sentences and set them free. But he never pardoned them, so their convictions stayed on the books and followed them everywhere.

Here’s what happened next.

**First:** the Department of Justice asked a federal appeals court to vacate those convictions once and for all.

**Then:** Rep. Jamie Raskin, one of the most partisan Democrats in Washington, D.C., filed a petition to block it. He opposed the DOJ in all three appeals and demanded the court appoint a special lawyer to defend the original jury verdicts. _His goal was to keep these Patriots branded as criminals for the rest of their lives_.

**That’s when Stand in the Gap Foundation stepped in.** We funded the defense team so they could answer Raskin on time and with strength. The attorneys worked through the weekend to meet a very tight deadline, and they filed.

**Now:** the convictions have been vacated and the cases dismissed. Raskin’s effort to keep the old verdicts alive did not stop it.

They tried to stop it. They failed.

That’s a victory worth celebrating. But it isn’t the end of the story...

[They need your help to rebuild their lives, which is exactly what Stand in the Gap Foundation exists to do. You can show your support by donating today.](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
[Donate Now](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
Legal forgiveness is only the beginning.

A court order can wipe a conviction off the record, but it can’t pay back years of legal bills, restore lost careers, or rebuild a reputation the media spent half a decade destroying.

These men and women walked out of prison financially drained, publicly smeared as _“insurrectionists”_ and _“terrorists,”_ and starting over from nothing.

**Stand in the Gap Foundation exists for this moment. Your gift today helps us:**
>>> Cover remaining legal costs so no Patriot is left defenseless against the next attack;

>>> Relieve the crushing debt left behind by years of litigation; and

>>> Provide reentry support so these Americans can find stable housing, return to work, and rebuild their lives.
The radical Left lost in court.

**_But if these Patriots are left broke and broken, the Left still gets what it wanted_.**

We can’t let that happen, Patriot.

[Please stand with us today and help give J6ers their futures back once and for all.](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
[Donate $10](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)

[Donate $35](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)

[Donate $1,000](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)

[Donate Any Other Amount](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
Even if you can’t give right now, your prayers for these patriots—for wisdom, strength, and protection—are powerful and deeply appreciated.

Many of our brothers and sisters are struggling to rebuild their lives even after receiving commuted sentences from President Trump.
**Stand in the Gap was created for this moment:** To resurrect their future after being continuously attacked and defamed.
We survive on your generous assistance. Without your rapid support, these individuals won’t have the legal resources they need to defend themselves effectively.

Thank you for your time, consideration, and continued support of conservative values and American justice.

[Your donation today provides emergency legal defense funding so we can keep standing strong and fighting for them.](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
[Donate](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
In solidarity,
Sarah McAbee
Co-Founder, Stand in the Gap

body:
# [](https://act.tammybaldwin.com/go/3095?t=1&akid=5853%2E35263%2Ep9eKei)
Peter,
Growing up, I watched firsthand how a serious medical problem could upend a family’s life — not just in pain and worry, but in the crushing bills and impossible choices that followed.
After I was diagnosed with a serious illness and spent three months in the hospital, my pre-existing condition prevented me from having health care.
**That’s why I’ve spent my career fighting to make health care accessible and affordable for Wisconsin families.**
Now, families are facing looming Medicaid cuts that republicans pushed through to pay for their disastrous so-called “Big Beautiful Bill”.
The stakes are high. More than 1.2 million Wisconsinites are enrolled in BadgerCare, including about one in three children in both our rural and metro communities. More than 20,000 Wisconsinites rely on Medicaid for opioid addiction treatment, and these cuts put their path to recovery at risk.
Rural hospitals depend on Medicaid to keep their doors open — so I offered an amendment to protect rural health care from these cuts — which Republicans rejected.
H.R. 1 is now law, and its effects are already reaching our families: parents of kids with disabilities, rural clinics worried about their budgets, and neighbors who are scared of losing coverage. I’m going to keep fighting for them, but I need everyone standing with me.
**[Will you add your name to our petition today?](https://act.tammybaldwin.com/signup/stop_medicaid_cuts?source=20261123-5853&t=2&akid=5853%2E35263%2Ep9eKei)** We’re showing Congress that they need to reverse the Medicaid cuts in H.R. 1, protect our rural hospitals and clinics, and keep health care within reach for every Wisconsin family.
**[Add your name ››](https://act.tammybaldwin.com/signup/stop_medicaid_cuts?source=20261123-5853&t=3&akid=5853%2E35263%2Ep9eKei)**
Thank you,
Tammy Baldwin

clean_body: Peter, Growing up, I watched firsthand how a serious medical problem could upend a family’s life — not just in pain and worry, but in the crushing bills and impossible choices that followed. After I was diagnosed with a serious illness and spent three months in the hospital, my pre-existing condition prevented me from having health care. That’s why I’ve spent my career fighting to make health care accessible and affordable for Wisconsin families. Now, families are facing looming Medicaid cuts that republicans pushed through to pay for their disastrous so-called “Big Beautiful Bill”. The stakes are high. More than 1.2 million Wisconsinites are enrolled in BadgerCare, including about one in three children in both our rural and metro communities. More than 20,000 Wisconsinites rely on Medicaid for opioid addiction treatment, and these cuts put their path to recovery at risk. Rural hospitals depend on Medicaid to keep their doors open — so I offered an amendment to protect rural health care from these cuts — which Republicans rejected. H.R. 1 is now law, and its effects are already reaching our families: parents of kids with disabilities, rural clinics worried about their budgets, and neighbors who are scared of losing coverage. I’m going to keep fighting for them, but I need everyone standing with me. We’re showing Congress that they need to reverse the Medicaid cuts in H.R. 1, protect our rural hospitals and clinics, and keep health care within reach for every Wisconsin family. Thank you, Tammy Baldwin

body:
[1]Justice Democrats

Peter,

Long before this November’s elections, AIPAC caught on to the fact that
their support is a toxic kiss of death to Democratic candidates running
for Congress.

But that didn’t stop the country’s largest pro-Israel lobby group from
spending $84 million in the 2026 midterms — they just found shady ways to
do it without tipping off voters.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20261123.66W-r-&refcode=em20261123-38448&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1002&akid=38448%2E1203867%2EGszCnm ]@lukewgoldstein: NEW: the midterms are awash in a new form of secretive
spending paid for by donors which aren't disclosed until after election
day. Much of it traces back to AIPAC, crypto, and Al. These lobbies have
found a way to launder their money through outside groups and shell PACs
to spend under the guise of progressive causes

In this year’s primaries, many of our corporate-backed opponents were
being supported by new, vaguely named pop-up PACs like Elect Democratic
Women and Pro-Choice Majority Action.

For example, in Chicago, shell PACs called Elect Chicago Women and
Affordable Chicago Now spent millions against JD-endorsed progressive Kat
Abughazaleh.

At the time, we suspected they were front groups for AIPAC and its super
PAC, United Democracy Project, to discreetly spend money in key races
without drawing attention to themselves. Now, it’s been confirmed.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20261123.66W-r-&refcode=em20261123-38448&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1003&akid=38448%2E1203867%2EGszCnm ]@brendan_fischer: Two pop-up super PACs that spent big in Illinois
Democratic primaries, Elect Chicago Women and Affordable Chicago Now, just
filed termination paperwork with the FEC, and transferred all of their
remaining funds back to the United Democracy Project.

Fork found in kitchen.

This is a misleading method for AIPAC’s far-right billionaire megadonors
to continue funneling financial support to their candidates of choice, and
those candidates can technically claim they don’t take AIPAC money.

By doing this, they’re deceiving the American public, and it’s only going
to get worse now that AIPAC announced they’re ending congressional
endorsements and direct contributions altogether.

As we prepare for the 2028 cycle, we’re keeping our eyes on UDP and the
pass-through PACs it will use to attack our progressive candidates and
funnel AIPAC megadonor money to pro-war, pro-genocide Democrats.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20261123.66W-r-&refcode=em20261123-38448&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1004&akid=38448%2E1203867%2EGszCnm ]We need you to help build up our resources and get ready to fight back:
chip in $5 or whatever you can spare to Justice Democrats
now!

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20261123.66W-r-&refcode=em20261123-38448&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1023&akid=38448%2E1203867%2EGszCnm ]Contribute $5

In solidarity,

Justice Democrats
